name: CHA₂DS₂-VASc Score
whenToUse: Patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation to assess annual stroke risk and need for anticoagulation.
whyUse: Widely validated; guideline-recommended (AHA/ACC/HRS, ESC) for stroke risk stratification in AF.

actions: Start or continue DOAC unless contraindicated
Check CBC, renal/hepatic function before DOAC
Educate on adherence and bleeding signs
Generally no anticoagulation for men with 0

name: HAS-BLED Score
whenToUse: Patients with AF being considered for or already on oral anticoagulation to estimate bleeding risk.
whyUse: Identifies modifiable bleeding risks; high score is not an automatic reason to withhold anticoagulation.

actions: Review and modify BP, alcohol, concomitant antiplatelets/NSAIDs
Ensure indication for OAC remains strong
High HAS-BLED alone should not preclude indicated anticoagulation

name: HEART Score for Major Cardiac Events
whenToUse: ED patients ≥21 years with chest pain concerning for ACS.
whyUse: Simple bedside score that identifies low-risk patients who may be candidates for early discharge.

actions: Consider discharge if serial exams/troponins reassuring
Stress testing or CTA as appropriate

name: TIMI Risk Score (UA/NSTEMI)
whenToUse: Patients with unstable angina or NSTEMI.
whyUse: Guides intensity of therapy and early invasive vs conservative strategies.

actions: Early invasive angiography (≤24–72h based on risk)

name: TIMI Risk Score (STEMI)
whenToUse: Patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
whyUse: Simple bedside mortality risk estimate for counseling and resource planning.

actions: Monitor for shock, arrhythmia, mechanical complications

name: GRACE Score (Simplified ACS)
whenToUse: UA, NSTEMI, or STEMI for mortality risk stratification.
whyUse: Guideline-endorsed comprehensive ACS risk model.

name: Killip Classification
whenToUse: Patients with acute myocardial infarction to grade HF severity.
whyUse: Classic bedside prognostic tool; still used in GRACE and clinical practice.

name: Wells Criteria for PE
whenToUse: Patients with suspected pulmonary embolism.
whyUse: Guides D-dimer vs imaging pathway.

actions: CT pulmonary angiography (or V/Q if CT contraindicated)
Consider empiric anticoagulation if high suspicion and low bleed risk while awaiting imaging

name: Wells Criteria for DVT
whenToUse: Suspected lower extremity DVT.
whyUse: Combined with D-dimer to safely rule out DVT.

actions: If positive, start anticoagulation if no contraindication

name: PERC Rule for PE
whenToUse: Low pretest probability PE patients (clinician gestalt <15%).
whyUse: Avoids unnecessary D-dimer and imaging in very low-risk patients.

actions: Do not use PERC alone to exclude PE
Apply Wells + D-dimer or imaging pathway

name: Revised Geneva Score (PE)
whenToUse: Suspected PE when an objective alternative to Wells is preferred.
whyUse: No subjective “PE most likely” item; fully standardized.

name: PESI (Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index)
whenToUse: Risk stratify confirmed acute PE for outpatient vs inpatient management.
whyUse: Identifies low-risk PE candidates for early discharge.

actions: Consider outpatient anticoagulation if reliable follow-up
Ensure no RV strain/other high-risk features
Assess for intermediate-high/high-risk PE (RV dysfunction, troponin, shock)

name: Simplified PESI (sPESI)
whenToUse: Rapid risk stratification of acute PE.
whyUse: Easier than full PESI with similar discrimination for low-risk PE.

name: CHADS₂ Score
whenToUse: Historical/educational use; prefer CHA₂DS₂-VASc in current practice.
whyUse: Still referenced in literature; simple five-factor model.

name: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)
whenToUse: Shock, hypertension emergencies, ICU titration of pressors.
whyUse: MAP better reflects tissue perfusion pressure than SBP alone.

name: Corrected QT (Bazett)
whenToUse: Drug monitoring, syncope, electrolyte disorders, congenital LQTS screening.
whyUse: Prolonged QTc increases risk of torsades de pointes.

actions: MgSO4 if TdP or very high risk

name: ASCVD 10-Year Risk (Pooled Cohort, simplified)
whenToUse: Adults 40–79 without prior ASCVD for primary prevention.
whyUse: ACC/AHA guideline tool for statin and aspirin discussions.

actions: Assess risk enhancers (family hx, Lp(a), CKD, etc.)

name: Centor Score (Modified / McIsaac)
whenToUse: Patients with sore throat to decide on rapid strep testing / culture.
whyUse: Reduces unnecessary antibiotics for viral pharyngitis.

actions: Treat confirmed GAS with penicillin/amoxicillin if no allergy

name: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)
whenToUse: Altered mental status, trauma, ICU sedation assessment.
whyUse: Universal language for neurologic status and triage.

actions: Urgent CT head if trauma/unknown cause

name: qSOFA Score
whenToUse: Outside ICU, patients with suspected infection.
whyUse: Simple screen for organ dysfunction risk; not a diagnostic criteria for sepsis alone.

actions: Blood cultures before antibiotics if no delay

name: SOFA Score
whenToUse: ICU patients, especially suspected sepsis, to track organ dysfunction.
whyUse: Sepsis-3 defines organ dysfunction as acute change in SOFA ≥2.

name: SIRS Criteria
whenToUse: Educational/historical; still used in some pathways as infection screen.
whyUse: Sensitive but non-specific; replaced by SOFA for sepsis definition.

actions: Evaluate for sepsis with lactate, cultures

name: NEWS2 Score
whenToUse: Hospitalized adults for routine observation and escalation.
whyUse: Standardized track-and-trigger system (NHS).

name: MEWS (Modified Early Warning Score)
whenToUse: Ward patients to detect clinical deterioration.
whyUse: Predecessor/alternative to NEWS used in many hospitals.

name: CURB-65 Score
whenToUse: Adults with community-acquired pneumonia for site-of-care decisions.
whyUse: Simple 5-variable score endorsed by BTS guidelines.

name: PSI / PORT Score (Pneumonia)
whenToUse: Adult CAP risk stratification when more detail than CURB-65 is desired.
whyUse: Highly validated; Classes I–II often outpatient candidates.

name: APACHE II (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Educational approximation of ICU mortality risk.
whyUse: Classic ICU severity score; full APACHE II needs 12 physiologic variables.

name: Revised Trauma Score (RTS)
whenToUse: Field or ED trauma triage and prognosis.
whyUse: Component of TRISS; correlates with survival.

name: A–a Oxygen Gradient
whenToUse: ABG interpretation for hypoxemia differential.
whyUse: Distinguishes V/Q mismatch, shunt, diffusion vs hypoventilation/low FiO₂.

name: PaO₂/FiO₂ Ratio (P/F)
whenToUse: Hypoxemic respiratory failure / ARDS assessment.
whyUse: Berlin definition severity tiers based on P/F with PEEP ≥5.

name: Ottawa Ankle Rules
whenToUse: Acute ankle or midfoot injury (<10 days) in patients ≥2–18+ years (validated adults).
whyUse: Safely reduces unnecessary radiographs.

actions: Ankle series and/or foot series as indicated

name: Ottawa Knee Rules
whenToUse: Acute knee injury.
whyUse: Reduces unnecessary knee films with high sensitivity.

name: NEXUS C-Spine Criteria
whenToUse: Blunt trauma patients for C-spine clearance.
whyUse: Avoids unnecessary C-spine imaging.

name: Canadian C-Spine Rule
whenToUse: Alert (GCS 15) stable adults with blunt trauma.
whyUse: Slightly more sensitive/specific than NEXUS in some comparisons.

name: Parkland Burn Formula
whenToUse: Adults/children with major burns needing formal resuscitation.
whyUse: Classic crystalloid estimate; give half in first 8 hours from injury time.

actions: Transfer to burn center per ABA criteria

name: Rule of Nines (Adult TBSA)
whenToUse: Adult burn TBSA estimation for Parkland and transfer criteria.
whyUse: Rapid field estimate; Lund-Browder better for children.

name: APGAR Score
whenToUse: Immediately after birth at 1 and 5 minutes (and q5 min if <7).
whyUse: Standard communication of newborn transition; not used alone to guide resuscitation start.

name: Bishop Score
whenToUse: Before labor induction to predict success.
whyUse: Low score may benefit from cervical ripening.

actions: Mechanical or prostaglandin ripening per protocol

name: Gestational Age & Naegele Due Date
whenToUse: Dating pregnancy when LMP known (ultrasound preferred early).
whyUse: Naegele’s rule standard estimate.

actions: Offer dating ultrasound if uncertain LMP

name: Pediatric GCS
whenToUse: Altered consciousness in infants/young children.
whyUse: Verbal component modified for developmental stage.

name: Westley Croup Score
whenToUse: Children with croup to guide treatment intensity.
whyUse: Standard severity tool in croup studies (dexamethasone/epinephrine).

name: PECARN Head Injury (Simplified)
whenToUse: Children with minor blunt head trauma (GCS 14–15).
whyUse: Identifies very low risk for ciTBI who may avoid CT.

name: 4Ts Score for HIT
whenToUse: Thrombocytopenia in patients receiving heparin.
whyUse: Guides whether to order HIT antibody testing and stop heparin.

name: Padua Prediction Score (VTE Risk)
whenToUse: Hospitalized medical patients for VTE prophylaxis decisions.
whyUse: Identifies high-risk medical inpatients (≥4).

actions: LMWH/heparin prophylaxis if bleed risk acceptable

name: Caprini Score (VTE Risk)
whenToUse: Perioperative VTE risk assessment.
whyUse: Widely used in surgical pathways for prophylaxis intensity.

actions: Extended prophylaxis after some orthopedic cases

name: STOP-BANG Sleep Apnea Screen
whenToUse: Preoperative or primary care OSA screening.
whyUse: Simple high-sensitivity screen.

name: Epworth Sleepiness Scale
whenToUse: Evaluation of excessive daytime sleepiness.
whyUse: Common patient-reported sleepiness measure.

name: BODE Index (COPD)
whenToUse: COPD prognostication and transplant referral discussions.
whyUse: Predicts mortality better than FEV1 alone.

name: Corticosteroid Conversion
whenToUse: Switching between systemic corticosteroids.
whyUse: Approximate anti-inflammatory equivalences.

name: Morphine Milligram Equivalents (MME)
whenToUse: Assessing opioid dose intensity and overdose risk.
whyUse: CDC thresholds (e.g., ≥50 MME/day) flag higher risk.

actions: Consider taper if harm outweighs benefit

name: Corrected Phenytoin (Albumin)
whenToUse: Total phenytoin levels with low albumin (or CrCl <20 with adjusted formula).
whyUse: Free phenytoin preferred; correction approximates when free level unavailable.

name: Transferrin Saturation
whenToUse: Iron deficiency vs overload assessment.
whyUse: Quick iron availability metric.

actions: Ferritin, HFE genetic testing as indicated

name: Predicted Sodium Change (Adrogue)
whenToUse: Planning correction of hypo/hypernatremia with IV fluids.
whyUse: Estimates ΔNa per liter to avoid overcorrection.

name: Modified Duke Criteria (IE Helper)
whenToUse: Suspected infective endocarditis classification.
whyUse: Standard diagnostic framework (definite / possible / rejected).

actions: Multiple blood cultures before antibiotics if stable

name: Jones Criteria (Acute Rheumatic Fever)
whenToUse: Suspected acute rheumatic fever.
whyUse: WHO/AHA diagnostic framework.

name: FeverPAIN Score
whenToUse: Acute sore throat antibiotic decision support.
whyUse: Predicts bacterial (strep) probability; guides delayed Rx strategies.

actions: Immediate Abx or RADT per local policy

name: Framingham Heart Failure Criteria
whenToUse: Clinical diagnosis of heart failure (historical/epidemiologic criteria).
whyUse: Classic major/minor framework still taught clinically.

name: NYHA Functional Classification
whenToUse: Staging functional limitation in known HF.
whyUse: Guides therapy intensity and trial eligibility language.

name: Expected PaO₂ (Age)
whenToUse: ABG interpretation on room air.
whyUse: PaO₂ normally declines with age.

name: Corrected QT (Fridericia)
whenToUse: QT correction when HR is very high or low.
whyUse: More accurate than Bazett at heart rate extremes.

name: Anion Gap Including Potassium
whenToUse: When comparing to lab AG methods that include K.
whyUse: Avoid misinterpretation of method differences.

name: Ideal Body Weight (Hamwi)
whenToUse: Alternative IBW estimate for nutrition.
whyUse: Common dietetics formula.

name: Corrected Calcium (SI units)
whenToUse: Labs reporting SI units.
whyUse: Avoid unit confusion with US conventional formula.

name: Child-Pugh Score
whenToUse: Cirrhosis severity, surgical risk, prognosis discussions.
whyUse: Classic liver disease staging; complements MELD for transplant.

name: MELD Score
whenToUse: Liver transplant prioritization and cirrhosis prognosis.
whyUse: Objective lab-based score used by transplant systems (often MELD-Na).

name: MELD-Na Score
whenToUse: Liver allocation / prognosis with hyponatremia.
whyUse: Hyponatremia adds prognostic information beyond MELD.

name: Glasgow-Blatchford Score (GBS)
whenToUse: Adults with suspected upper GI bleeding.
whyUse: Score 0 identifies very low-risk patients safe for outpatient management.

actions: Consider discharge with early GI follow-up

name: Rockall Score (Pre-endoscopy)
whenToUse: Upper GI bleed mortality risk stratification.
whyUse: Complements GBS; full Rockall includes endoscopic findings.

name: Alvarado Score (Appendicitis)
whenToUse: Suspected appendicitis to guide imaging/surgery decisions.
whyUse: Structured clinical probability; imaging still common.

name: BISAP Score
whenToUse: Early severity assessment in acute pancreatitis (first 24h).
whyUse: Simple, uses data available early; predicts mortality.

name: ABCD² Score
whenToUse: Patients with recent TIA symptoms.
whyUse: Guides urgency of workup (though urgent workup increasingly universal).

name: NIH Stroke Scale (Simplified Total)
whenToUse: Acute ischemic stroke severity and communication.
whyUse: Standard for tPA/thrombectomy trials and serial exams.

name: PHQ-9 Depression Screen
whenToUse: Screening and monitoring major depression in primary care and specialty settings.
whyUse: Validated, brief, and widely integrated into workflows.

name: GAD-7 Anxiety Screen
whenToUse: Screening and severity monitoring for generalized anxiety.
whyUse: Brief, validated anxiety measure.

name: CAGE Questionnaire
whenToUse: Primary care / ED screening for problem drinking.
whyUse: Very brief four-question screen.

name: CIWA-Ar (Alcohol Withdrawal)
whenToUse: Symptom-triggered benzodiazepine protocols for alcohol withdrawal.
whyUse: Standard severity score guiding benzo dosing.

name: MMSE (Score Entry)
whenToUse: Cognitive screening interpretation when MMSE already administered.
whyUse: Widely known cognitive screen (copyrighted instrument — enter total only).

name: MoCA (Score Entry)
whenToUse: Interpretation of administered MoCA total.
whyUse: More sensitive than MMSE for mild cognitive impairment.

name: Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI)
whenToUse: Adults undergoing noncardiac surgery for preoperative cardiac risk stratification.
whyUse: Simple, validated 6-factor index used widely in perioperative medicine and guidelines.

actions: Focus on guideline-directed medical therapy and surgical recovery
Consider additional testing only if it will change management

name: CRB-65 Score
whenToUse: Adults with community-acquired pneumonia when BUN/urea is unavailable (e.g., clinic or prehospital).
whyUse: Bedside alternative to CURB-65 for site-of-care decisions without blood tests.

name: SMART-COP Score
whenToUse: Adults with CAP to estimate risk of needing IRVS (ICU-level support).
whyUse: Better identifies ICU need than CURB-65 alone in some cohorts.

actions: Usual ward or outpatient pathway as otherwise indicated

name: mMRC Dyspnea Scale
whenToUse: COPD and chronic respiratory disease to grade dyspnea-related disability.
whyUse: Simple patient-reported grade used in GOLD ABE assessment and symptom burden.

actions: Combine with exacerbation history for GOLD ABE grouping

name: SpO₂/FiO₂ Ratio (S/F)
whenToUse: Hypoxemic respiratory failure when arterial blood gas is unavailable or for serial noninvasive monitoring.
whyUse: S/F correlates with P/F; useful triage and ARDS screening without ABG.

name: EDACS (Emergency Department Assessment of Chest Pain Score)
whenToUse: ED patients with possible cardiac chest pain in accelerated diagnostic protocols.
whyUse: Identifies low-risk patients (with negative ECG/troponins) safe for early discharge.

name: ATRIA Bleeding Risk Score
whenToUse: Patients with AF on or considering warfarin to stratify major hemorrhage risk.
whyUse: Simple score from a large ATRIA cohort; complements stroke risk assessment.

name: SAMe-TT₂R₂ Score
whenToUse: Patients with AF being considered for warfarin vs DOAC when TTR quality is a concern.
whyUse: Identifies who is less likely to achieve good INR control on VKA—favor DOAC if eligible.

actions: If VKA mandatory, frequent INR checks and adherence support

name: Sgarbossa Criteria (MI in LBBB)
whenToUse: Suspected ACS with LBBB (or ventricular paced rhythm in adapted use) when STEMI diagnosis is uncertain.
whyUse: Highly specific criteria for occlusion MI when concordant changes are present.

name: Duke Treadmill Score
whenToUse: Patients undergoing Bruce-protocol exercise ECG for suspected CAD prognosis.
whyUse: Stratifies annual cardiovascular mortality; guides need for angiography.

actions: Consider stress imaging or coronary CTA

name: Berlin ARDS Definition Helper
whenToUse: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure evaluation for ARDS diagnosis and severity.
whyUse: Standard international definition guiding lung-protective strategies and trial eligibility.

actions: Specialty center / ECMO evaluation if refractory

name: Heffner Criteria (Pleural Effusion)
whenToUse: When serum protein/LDH simultaneous values are unavailable, or as a simplified adjunct to Light’s.
whyUse: Uses pleural fluid values alone; practical when paired serum labs are missing.

actions: Cell count, culture, cytology as indicated
Correlate with Light’s when serum labs available

name: Cardiac Power Output
whenToUse: Cardiogenic shock or advanced HF with measured/estimated CO and MAP available.
whyUse: Strong hemodynamic correlate of prognosis in cardiogenic shock (e.g., SHOCK trial analyses).

name: Age-Adjusted Shock Index
whenToUse: Trauma, sepsis, or hemorrhage triage when occult shock is a concern, especially in older adults.
whyUse: Age adjustment improves prediction of mortality/transfusion need vs raw shock index in some studies.

actions: IV access, labs, imaging as indicated

name: Framingham-Style 10-Year Hard CHD Risk (Educational)
whenToUse: Adult primary-prevention teaching / rough risk orientation when a full official calculator is unavailable.
whyUse: Illustrates how traditional risk factors combine; for clinical decisions use validated ACC/AHA PREVENT or PCE tools.

actions: Address smoking, BP, lipids, weight, activity
Shared decision-making on statin/antihypertensive therapy per guidelines

name: Canadian CT Head Rule
whenToUse: Adults with minor head injury: witnessed LOC, amnesia, or disorientation; GCS 13–15. Not for age <16, blood thinners, or seizure after injury.
whyUse: High sensitivity for neurosurgical lesions and clinically important brain injury while reducing unnecessary CT.

actions: Consider observation or discharge with precautions if no other concern

name: New Orleans / Charter CT Head Criteria
whenToUse: Patients with minor head injury and GCS 15 who had LOC or amnesia.
whyUse: Very sensitive for intracranial injury; more liberal (less specific) than Canadian CT Head Rule.

actions: Clinical clearance if GCS remains 15 and reliable

name: YEARS Algorithm for PE
whenToUse: Hemodynamically stable patients with suspected PE in whom D-dimer-based exclusion is appropriate.
whyUse: Raises D-dimer threshold to 1000 ng/mL when no YEARS items present, reducing imaging without major miss rate.

actions: Treat if high pretest and delay to imaging in selected cases

name: San Francisco Syncope Rule (CHESS)
whenToUse: Adult ED patients with syncope or near-syncope for short-term serious outcome risk.
whyUse: Simple high-sensitivity screen; any positive criterion = higher risk.

name: Canadian Syncope Risk Score
whenToUse: Adult ED patients with syncope once a serious cause is not already evident on index evaluation.
whyUse: Stratifies 30-day risk of arrhythmia, MI, structural issues, and death better than CHESS alone in validations.

actions: Primary care / cardiology follow-up as needed
Shared decision for observation vs discharge

name: Hestia Criteria (Outpatient PE)
whenToUse: Confirmed acute PE when considering home treatment vs admission.
whyUse: If all answers are “no,” outpatient management is often safe in validated cohorts (with clinical judgment).

name: Ottawa Foot Rules
whenToUse: Acute midfoot injury; reliable exam (typically within 10 days of injury).
whyUse: High sensitivity for clinically significant midfoot fractures; reduces unnecessary films.

name: Modified Mallampati Classification
whenToUse: Pre-intubation or pre-sedation airway assessment (patient sitting, mouth open, tongue out, no phonation).
whyUse: Quick component of multivariable difficult-airway assessment (e.g., LEMON); alone has limited predictive value.

name: Shock Index
whenToUse: Trauma, hemorrhage risk, sepsis, or any undifferentiated illness when occult hypoperfusion is a concern.
whyUse: May rise before frank hypotension; correlates with transfusion need, lactate, and mortality in several cohorts.

name: START Triage Helper
whenToUse: Multi-casualty / disaster scenes using START adult triage logic.
whyUse: Rapid categorization into Minor, Delayed, Immediate, or Expectant/Deceased to prioritize resources.

name: NEXUS Chest Decision Rule
whenToUse: Blunt trauma patients ≥15 years being considered for chest X-ray or chest CT.
whyUse: If all criteria absent, very low risk of clinically significant thoracic injury; imaging may be avoided.

actions: Omit routine chest imaging if appropriate
CXR or CT based on severity

name: LRINEC Score
whenToUse: Suspected necrotizing soft tissue infection when labs are available; adjunct only.
whyUse: Helps risk-stratify; low score does not rule out NSTI if clinical suspicion is high.

name: Baux Score (Burn Mortality)
whenToUse: Major burns for rapid prognostic estimate and burn-center communication.
whyUse: Simple mortality correlate; revised Baux adds inhalation injury weight.

name: Abbreviated Burn Severity Index (ABSI)
whenToUse: Acute burn evaluation for severity stratification and prognosis communication.
whyUse: Incorporates depth and inhalation beyond simple Baux; maps to rough survival bands.

actions: Transfer if other ABA criteria met

name: LEMON Difficult Airway Assessment
whenToUse: Before RSI or elective intubation to anticipate difficult airway.
whyUse: Structured mnemonic prompts preparation of equipment, personnel, and backup plans.

actions: Help at bedside if high score

name: FIB-4 Index
whenToUse: Outpatient risk stratification for advanced fibrosis in viral hepatitis, NAFLD/MASLD, and other chronic liver disease.
whyUse: Simple labs; dual cutoffs triage who needs elastography/biopsy vs low-risk follow-up.

actions: Evaluate for cirrhosis complications if high

name: APRI Score
whenToUse: Noninvasive fibrosis staging aid, especially viral hepatitis and resource-limited settings.
whyUse: Uses only AST, AST ULN, and platelets; WHO-endorsed in some HCV pathways.

name: AIMS65 Score
whenToUse: Adults with acute upper GI bleeding for early mortality risk stratification.
whyUse: Five binary admission variables; easy bedside mortality estimate complementary to GBS/Rockall.

actions: Still apply GBS for discharge safety
Do not use AIMS65 alone for outpatient triage

name: Lille Model (Alcoholic Hepatitis)
whenToUse: Day 7 of corticosteroid therapy for severe alcoholic hepatitis (usually DF ≥32 or equivalent).
whyUse: Identifies non-responders (Lille ≥0.45) who may not benefit from continued steroids.

name: Glasgow Alcoholic Hepatitis Score (GAHS)
whenToUse: Alcoholic hepatitis severity assessment; score ≥9 associated with higher mortality.
whyUse: Uses age, WBC, urea, PT ratio/INR, and bilirubin; may outperform DF for mortality in some cohorts.

name: R-Factor for DILI
whenToUse: Suspected drug-induced liver injury to characterize biochemical pattern at presentation (or peak).
whyUse: Pattern guides differential (e.g., hepatocellular vs cholestatic drugs), causality assessment, and expected course.

name: Forrest Classification (Ulcer Bleed)
whenToUse: During or after endoscopy for bleeding peptic ulcer to describe stigmata and guide therapy/disposition.
whyUse: Standardizes rebleeding risk communication and need for endoscopic hemostasis / high-dose PPI.

name: Revised Atlanta Classification Helper
whenToUse: Classify acute pancreatitis severity using organ failure duration and local/systemic complications.
whyUse: Revised Atlanta (2012) is the consensus clinical severity framework guiding intensity of care.

actions: Cholecystectomy same admission if gallstone AP when suitable

name: Appendicitis Inflammatory Response (AIR) Score
whenToUse: Suspected appendicitis to stratify low vs high probability and guide imaging/surgery.
whyUse: Incorporates graded peritonitis and CRP; often better calibrated than Alvarado in validations.

name: RIPASA Appendicitis Score
whenToUse: Suspected acute appendicitis clinical probability estimation.
whyUse: Includes demographics, symptoms, signs, labs, and urinalysis; cutoff ≥7.5 often used for high sensitivity.

name: NAFLD Fibrosis Score
whenToUse: Patients with NAFLD/MASLD to estimate likelihood of bridging fibrosis/cirrhosis.
whyUse: Dual cutoffs identify low- and high-risk groups and reduce unnecessary biopsy.

name: Mayo Risk Score (PSC)
whenToUse: Prognostication in PSC using age, bilirubin, AST, albumin, and history of variceal bleeding.
whyUse: Estimates relative risk of death or transplant need; complements MELD for listing decisions.

name: Glasgow-Imrie Criteria (Pancreatitis)
whenToUse: Acute pancreatitis severity prediction during the first 48 hours of admission.
whyUse: Simple multi-parameter count; ≥3 criteria suggests predicted severe disease and higher-level monitoring.

name: KDIGO AKI Staging
whenToUse: Hospitalized patients with rising creatinine and/or oliguria to stage AKI severity.
whyUse: Standard international staging that guides monitoring intensity, nephrotoxin avoidance, and RRT planning.

actions: Bladder scan / post-void residual if obstruction possible

name: Bedside Schwartz Pediatric eGFR
whenToUse: Children ~1–16 years for CKD staging, drug dosing context, or renal function estimates.
whyUse: Preferred simple bedside pediatric eGFR with IDMS-traceable creatinine.

actions: Pediatric nephrology if progressive or low eGFR

name: PLASMIC Score (TTP / ADAMTS13)
whenToUse: Thrombotic microangiopathy when deciding urgency of plasma exchange pending ADAMTS13 activity.
whyUse: High scores support early caplacizumab/PEX pathway while low scores argue against severe TTP.

actions: ADAMTS13 activity before PEX if possible without delay
Broaden TMA differential (aHUS, DIC, malignant HTN, drugs)

name: ISTH Overt DIC Score
whenToUse: Patients with an underlying DIC-associated condition and abnormal coagulation tests.
whyUse: Standardized criteria for overt DIC diagnosis and serial monitoring.

actions: Treat underlying driver (sepsis, trauma, malignancy, obstetric)

name: Khorana Score (Cancer-Associated VTE)
whenToUse: Ambulatory solid tumor / lymphoma patients before or during systemic therapy for prophylaxis decisions.
whyUse: Identifies higher-risk oncology outpatients who may benefit from thromboprophylaxis discussion.

name: MASCC Risk Index (Febrile Neutropenia)
whenToUse: Adults with fever and neutropenia to risk-stratify complications.
whyUse: Score ≥21 predicts lower risk of serious medical complications and may support oral/step-down care.

actions: Consider oral regimen per protocol (e.g., cipro + amox-clav if no allergy/local resistance issues)

name: McIsaac Score (Modified Centor)
whenToUse: Acute pharyngitis to guide RADT/culture and antibiotic stewardship.
whyUse: Age adjustment improves discrimination versus classic Centor alone, especially at extremes of age.

actions: Penicillin/amoxicillin if GAS confirmed (or per allergy)

name: Classic Kawasaki Disease Criteria
whenToUse: Febrile children with possible mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome.
whyUse: Classic criteria support timely IVIG to reduce coronary artery complications.

name: Rochester Criteria (Febrile Infant)
whenToUse: Well-appearing febrile infants (historically ≤60 days) when applying classic low-risk labs.
whyUse: Educational/historical low-risk tool; modern practice often prefers PECARN/Step-by-Step/AAP pathways.

actions: Age-based full sepsis workup as indicated
Admission vs close observation per protocol
Reliable follow-up essential if observation strategy used

name: IMPROVE Bleeding Risk Score
whenToUse: Medical inpatients when balancing pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis against bleed risk.
whyUse: Identifies higher bleeding risk (≥7 often used) to favor mechanical prophylaxis or closer monitoring.

name: Delta Gap / Excess Anion Gap
whenToUse: High anion gap metabolic acidosis to screen for coexisting NAGMA or metabolic alkalosis.
whyUse: Delta-delta (excess AG + HCO₃) reveals mixed disorders missed by AG alone.

actions: Urine anion gap / NH4 if needed
Look for vomiting, diuretics, volume contraction, alkali
Lactate, ketones, toxic alcohols, renal function as indicated

name: Sodium Change with Infusate (Adrogué-Madias)
whenToUse: Planning IV fluid therapy for hypo- or hypernatremia.
whyUse: Estimates ΔNa per liter to design safer correction rates and reduce ODS risk.

name: Transtubular Potassium Gradient (TTKG)
whenToUse: Educational evaluation of renal K handling in hypo/hyperkalemia when urine is concentrated.
whyUse: Classic teaching aid for mineralocorticoid effect; limited validity with modern understanding of urea and flow.

name: Fractional Excretion of Magnesium (FEMg)
whenToUse: Hypomagnesemia workup when deciding renal vs GI losses.
whyUse: Accounts for protein-bound Mg (~30% bound → ultrafilterable fraction ~0.7).

name: SOFA Delta (Sepsis-3 Organ Dysfunction)
whenToUse: Patients with suspected infection when applying Sepsis-3 clinical criteria.
whyUse: Sepsis-3 defines organ dysfunction as an acute increase in SOFA ≥2 points attributable to infection.

actions: Cultures before abx if no delay

name: Pediatric Early Warning Score (PEWS, simplified)
whenToUse: Hospitalized children for track-and-trigger monitoring of clinical deterioration.
whyUse: Standardized bedside escalation tool; exact tables vary by institution — this is an educational simplification.

name: HEMORR₂HAGES Bleeding Risk Score
whenToUse: Patients on or considered for anticoagulation when quantifying bleeding risk factors.
whyUse: Includes prior bleed double-weighting and geriatric/comorbidity factors; highlights modifiable risks.

name: ORBIT Bleeding Risk Score (AF)
whenToUse: AF patients on oral anticoagulation for major bleeding risk estimation.
whyUse: Simple five-factor score with good calibration in ORBIT-AF; emphasizes anemia and prior bleed.

name: Hunt and Hess Grade (SAH)
whenToUse: Patients with suspected or confirmed subarachnoid hemorrhage for clinical severity grading.
whyUse: Classic bedside grade linked to surgical risk and outcomes; complements Fisher/modified Fisher imaging grades.

actions: Urgent noncontrast CT ± LP if CT negative and suspicion high
BP control, reverse anticoagulation, nimodipine, seizure precautions per protocol

name: Modified Fisher CT Grade (SAH)
whenToUse: CT assessment of aneurysmal SAH to estimate delayed cerebral ischemia / vasospasm risk.
whyUse: Modified Fisher accounts for thick cisternal blood and IVH combinations that drive vasospasm risk.

actions: Neuro ICU monitoring for DCI (days 3–14 typical peak)
Low threshold for TCD / perfusion imaging if exam changes

name: ICH Score
whenToUse: Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage prognosis discussions and risk stratification.
whyUse: Simple, validated 0–6 score correlating with 30-day mortality.

actions: Neurosurgery consult (posterior fossa, hydrocephalus, selected supratentorial)
Avoid early nihilism based on score alone

name: Modified Rankin Scale (mRS)
whenToUse: Baseline and follow-up functional status after stroke or neurologic injury.
whyUse: Universal ordinal disability scale for prognosis discussions and research endpoints (often mRS 0–2 = good outcome).

name: FOUR Score (Full Outline of UnResponsiveness)
whenToUse: Altered consciousness in ICU/neurocritical care, especially intubated patients (no verbal component needed).
whyUse: Captures brainstem reflexes and respiratory pattern missing from GCS; total 0–16.

name: PHQ-2 Depression Screen
whenToUse: Ultra-brief depression screening in primary care, ED, and specialty clinics.
whyUse: High sensitivity gateway screen; positives should proceed to PHQ-9 or clinical interview.

actions: Do not rely on screen alone

name: AUDIT-C Alcohol Screen
whenToUse: Brief alcohol misuse screening in primary care, trauma, and preoperative settings.
whyUse: Faster than full AUDIT with good sensitivity for hazardous drinking.

name: COWS (Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale)
whenToUse: Monitoring opioid withdrawal and guiding initiation of buprenorphine / supportive care.
whyUse: Standard bedside severity score for symptom-triggered opioid withdrawal management.

actions: Supportive meds (antiemetics, clonidine if appropriate, hydration)
Consider buprenorphine when COWS threshold met and last full agonist timing appropriate

name: SAD PERSONS Suicide Risk Scale
whenToUse: Structured reminder of suicide risk factors during psych evaluation (not a standalone disposition tool).
whyUse: Mnemonic covering classic risk factors; educational aid — clinical judgment always required.

actions: Do not discharge based on low checklist score alone

name: Mini-Cog
whenToUse: Rapid cognitive screening in primary care and geriatric assessment.
whyUse: Quick, relatively education-insensitive screen for cognitive impairment.

name: CAM-ICU Delirium Screen
whenToUse: Ventilated or non-ventilated ICU patients for bedside delirium screening.
whyUse: Validated ICU delirium tool; positives associate with longer stays and worse outcomes.

actions: Avoid routine antipsychotics for hypoactive delirium without distress

name: Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS)
whenToUse: ICU titration of sedation and assessment of agitation; input to CAM-ICU.
whyUse: Standard, reproducible target for light sedation strategies (often 0 to −2).

name: ASPECTS (Early Ischemic Change)
whenToUse: Noncontrast CT (or DWI-ASPECTS) in anterior circulation LVO / thrombolysis-thrombectomy pathways.
whyUse: Quantifies early ischemic change; lower scores suggest larger established infarct core.

actions: Do not delay CTA/CTP or transfer for ASPECTS calculation alone
Correlate with NIHSS and last known well

name: ABCD3-I Score (TIA)
whenToUse: Risk stratification after TIA when imaging and short-term recurrence history are available.
whyUse: Improves prediction of early stroke after TIA beyond ABCD² alone.

actions: Urgent brain and vascular imaging if not done
Carotid revascularization evaluation if appropriate stenosis

name: C-SSRS Screener (Simplified)
whenToUse: Structured suicide ideation/behavior screening in clinical settings.
whyUse: Widely adopted severity ladder from wish to die through intent/plan and recent behavior.

actions: Consider involuntary hold criteria per jurisdiction

name: MDQ (Mood Disorder Questionnaire)
whenToUse: Screening for bipolar spectrum disorder in primary care and mental health settings.
whyUse: Brief self-report screen; positives need diagnostic interview (not diagnostic alone).

actions: Avoid unopposed antidepressant if bipolar likely
Discuss mood stabilizer / atypical antipsychotic options with specialist as appropriate

name: Shock Index, Pediatric Adjusted (SIPA)
whenToUse: Injured children to identify need for transfusion, operative intervention, or ICU care.
whyUse: Age-adjusted SI outperforms adult SI cutoffs and vital signs alone in pediatric trauma.

actions: Continue standard trauma evaluation — normal SIPA does not exclude injury

name: Yale Observation Scale (Febrile Child)
whenToUse: Febrile children (classically 3–36 months) when assessing overall toxic appearance.
whyUse: Structures the “ill vs well” gestalt into reproducible observational domains.

name: Step-by-Step (Febrile Young Infant)
whenToUse: Well-appearing febrile infants 0–90 days when applying Step-by-Step risk stratification.
whyUse: Identifies infants at low risk of invasive bacterial infection who may avoid LP/admission in validated pathways.

actions: Pathway-directed observation or discharge with follow-up

name: VBAC Success (Grobman Educational Model)
whenToUse: Counseling candidates for trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC).
whyUse: Major predictors of VBAC success help shared decision-making; not a guarantee of outcome.

actions: Discuss uterine rupture (~0.5–1% after low transverse scar)

name: Preeclampsia Diagnostic Criteria Helper
whenToUse: Suspected preeclampsia after 20 weeks gestation (or postpartum).
whyUse: Structures diagnostic criteria including atypical presentations without proteinuria.

name: HELLP Syndrome Lab Pattern Helper
whenToUse: Suspected HELLP in pregnant/postpartum patients with preeclampsia features or RUQ pain.
whyUse: Organizes classic lab triad; incomplete HELLP still warrants aggressive management.

name: Magnesium Toxicity Levels Helper
whenToUse: Patients on MgSO₄ for preeclampsia/eclampsia or to interpret a Mg level.
whyUse: Links level ranges to loss of reflexes, respiratory depression, and cardiac risk.

nextSteps.condition: Loss of DTRs or respiratory depression

actions: q1h nursing checks: RR, SpO2, DTRs, UOP

name: Ethanol Level Estimate
whenToUse: Rough educational estimate of ethanol level when formal level delayed, or to relate osm gap to EtOH.
whyUse: Widmark and osm-gap conversions are common bedside approximations — not forensic measurements.

actions: Consider other alcohols if gap unexplained

name: Rumack-Matthew Time/Level Helper
whenToUse: Single acute acetaminophen ingestion ≥4 hours post-ingestion with a timed level.
whyUse: Approximates whether level is above the 150 treatment line for NAC decisions (educational).

name: Loading Dose Calculator
whenToUse: Estimating IV loading doses when Vd and target level are known (e.g., teaching PK).
whyUse: Core pharmacokinetic relationship for achieving steady concentration quickly.

name: Infusion Rate (mcg/kg/min → mL/hr)
whenToUse: Titrating vasoactive or other continuous infusions with known concentration.
whyUse: Prevents unit errors when programming pumps.

name: Corrected Reticulocyte Count & RPI
whenToUse: Anemia workup to distinguish hypo- vs hyperproliferative response.
whyUse: Raw retic % overestimates production when Hct is low; RPI accounts for shift/maturation.

name: Absolute Lymphocyte Count (ALC)
whenToUse: Infection risk, viral illness, immunodeficiency screens, chemo recovery.
whyUse: Absolute counts are more informative than percentages alone.

actions: Flow cytometry if persistent in adults

name: Sodium Deficit
whenToUse: Planning sodium replacement in symptomatic or severe hyponatremia (adjunct).
whyUse: Provides a rough total deficit estimate; correction rate limits are critical.

name: Expected PCO₂ (Metabolic Alkalosis)
whenToUse: Metabolic alkalosis to detect concurrent respiratory disorders.
whyUse: Compensation is hypoventilation; if PCO₂ differs from expected, mixed disorder likely.

name: Hypertonic Hyponatremia (Glucose Correction)
whenToUse: Hyponatremia with marked hyperglycemia (DKA/HHS) to estimate effective water balance.
whyUse: Translocational hyponatremia from glucose; corrected Na guides free-water status.

actions: Use corrected Na for fluid planning

name: Pediatric Ideal Body Weight
whenToUse: Weight-based dosing or nutrition estimates in children when IBW is preferred over total body weight.
whyUse: Traub-Johnson provides a simple height-based IBW used in pediatric pharmacy contexts.

actions: Consider adjusted body weight if obese per protocol

name: Finnegan NAS Score (Simplified)
whenToUse: Infants at risk for neonatal opioid withdrawal when Finnegan-style serial scoring is used.
whyUse: Structures CNS, metabolic/vasomotor, and GI withdrawal signs; thresholds guide treatment.

actions: Non-pharm first: swaddle, low stimulation, feeding support

name: Urine Anion Gap
whenToUse: Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis to help distinguish GI bicarb loss vs RTA.
whyUse: Negative UAG suggests appropriate NH₄⁺ excretion (e.g., diarrhea); positive suggests impaired renal acidification (RTA).

actions: K, Ca, growth (peds), autoimmune workup as indicated

name: Cockcroft-Gault CrCl
whenToUse: Drug dosing adjustments based on renal function.
whyUse: Still used in many FDA drug labels despite CKD-EPI for staging.

name: CKD-EPI Creatinine eGFR (2021)
whenToUse: CKD detection, staging, and monitoring.
whyUse: Preferred equation in current KDIGO/NKF guidance (2021 race-free).

actions: Prepare for RRT education if progressive

name: MDRD eGFR (4-variable)
whenToUse: Legacy reports; prefer CKD-EPI for new estimates.
whyUse: Still appears on older lab reports.

name: Fractional Excretion of Sodium (FENa)
whenToUse: Oliguric AKI when patient not on diuretics.
whyUse: Classic tool; limited if diuretics used (prefer FeUrea).

name: Fractional Excretion of Urea (FeUrea)
whenToUse: AKI on diuretics when FENa unreliable.
whyUse: Urea handling less affected by loop diuretics than sodium.

actions: Correlate with volume status and clinical course

name: Anion Gap (Serum)
whenToUse: Metabolic acidosis differential (HAGMA vs NAGMA).
whyUse: Core acid-base calculation.

actions: Lactate, ketones, toxic alcohols if indicated

name: Corrected Calcium
whenToUse: Hypoalbuminemia when ionized Ca not available.
whyUse: Rough estimate; ionized calcium preferred.

name: Corrected Sodium (Hyperglycemia)
whenToUse: Hyperglycemia, DKA, HHS to estimate true sodium.
whyUse: Hyperglycemia lowers measured Na; correction guides free water status.

actions: Use corrected Na for fluid planning

name: Calculated Serum Osmolality
whenToUse: Hyponatremia workup, toxic alcohol suspicion.
whyUse: Osmolal gap screens for methanol/ethylene glycol and other osmoles.

name: Osmolal Gap
whenToUse: Suspected toxic alcohol ingestion.
whyUse: Rapid screen while awaiting levels.

name: Free Water Deficit (Hypernatremia)
whenToUse: Hypernatremia fluid replacement planning.
whyUse: Guides free water replacement rate (avoid overly rapid correction).

actions: Prefer enteral free water if possible

name: Bicarbonate Deficit
whenToUse: Severe acidemia when bicarbonate therapy considered (selected cases).
whyUse: Rough dosing guide; treat underlying cause primarily.

name: Body Mass Index (BMI)
whenToUse: Weight classification and health risk counseling.
whyUse: Standard anthropometric index.

name: Ideal Body Weight (Devine)
whenToUse: Drug dosing (e.g., some antimicrobials), nutrition estimates.
whyUse: Common pharmacy standard.

actions: Calculate AdjBW = IBW + 0.4×(TBW−IBW) for selected drugs

name: Adjusted Body Weight
whenToUse: Obese patients for selected drug dosing.
whyUse: Accounts for partial distribution into adipose tissue.

actions: Confirm specific drug monograph for weight scalar

name: Body Surface Area (Mosteller)
whenToUse: Chemotherapy dosing, cardiac index, burn estimates adjunct.
whyUse: Mosteller is simple and widely accepted.

actions: Consider caps in obesity per protocol

name: Maintenance IV Fluids (4-2-1)
whenToUse: Maintenance fluid estimates for children and adults.
whyUse: Classic weight-based hourly rate.

actions: Use isotonic fluids with appropriate dextrose/K

name: HOMA-IR
whenToUse: Research/clinical estimate of insulin resistance (fasting labs).
whyUse: Simple surrogate without clamp studies.

name: eAG from HbA1c
whenToUse: Patient education linking A1c to average glucose.
whyUse: ADA-endorsed conversion from ADAG study.

name: LDL Cholesterol (Friedewald)
whenToUse: Standard lipid panel when TG <400 mg/dL.
whyUse: Most common calculated LDL method.

name: Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC)
whenToUse: Chemotherapy, febrile neutropenia risk, clozapine monitoring.
whyUse: Defines neutropenia severity.

name: HEART Pathway
whenToUse: ED patients with possible ACS when applying a HEART Pathway–style accelerated diagnostic protocol.
whyUse: Identifies very low-risk patients (HEART 0–3 + negative serial troponins) who may be eligible for early discharge.

actions: Do not early-discharge on pathway alone
Treat as possible ACS until proven otherwise

name: ADHERE Heart Failure Risk (Simplified Tree)
whenToUse: Adults hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure for early mortality risk stratification.
whyUse: Simple bedside tree from a large US registry; identifies low- vs high-risk groups using three variables.

name: EFFECT HF Mortality Score (Simplified)
whenToUse: Adults admitted with heart failure when estimating short-term mortality risk (educational/simplified).
whyUse: Highlights major EFFECT variables (age, vitals, labs, comorbidities) without full multi-outcome nomogram complexity.

name: GWTG-HF Risk Score (Simplified)
whenToUse: Adults admitted with acute HF for educational in-hospital mortality risk estimate.
whyUse: Based on major GWTG-HF predictors (age, SBP, BUN, sodium, heart rate, COPD, race).

name: Cerebral Performance Category (CPC)
whenToUse: Document neurologic outcome after cardiac arrest (research, prognostication discussions, discharge status).
whyUse: Standard Utstein-style outcome category used across resuscitation literature.

name: Stroke Volume & Ejection Fraction
whenToUse: When EDV and ESV are known from echocardiography, ventriculography, or other imaging.
whyUse: Fundamental relationships: SV = EDV − ESV; EF = SV/EDV; CO = SV × HR.

actions: Integrate with CI, lactate, filling pressures

name: Cardiac Index
whenToUse: When CO and BSA are known (PA catheter, echo estimates, pulse contour) for perfusion assessment.
whyUse: Indexes CO to body size; used in Forrester classification, shock algorithms, and transplant/MCS evaluation.

name: Systemic Vascular Resistance (SVR)
whenToUse: When MAP, CVP (or RAP), and CO are available to characterize vasomotor tone.
whyUse: Distinguishes vasodilatory vs vasoconstricted shock and guides pressor/vasodilator therapy.

name: Pulmonary Vascular Resistance (PVR)
whenToUse: Right heart catheterization interpretation for pulmonary hypertension and transplant evaluation.
whyUse: Defines precapillary component of PH; guides PAH vs left-heart disease physiology.

actions: Referral to PH center as indicated

name: Corrected QT (Framingham)
whenToUse: QT correction when an alternative to Bazett/Fridericia is desired; Framingham performs well across HR ranges.
whyUse: Linear formula derived from Framingham Heart Study; less HR-biased than Bazett at extremes.

name: Corrected QT (Hodges)
whenToUse: QT correction with a linear heart-rate formula alternative to Bazett.
whyUse: Simple linear correction; often better than Bazett at high/low HR.

name: Tisdale QTc Prolongation Risk Score
whenToUse: Hospitalized adults starting QT-prolonging drugs or with multiple TdP risk factors.
whyUse: Validated score to identify patients at low/moderate/high risk of QTc >500 ms or large QTc increase.

actions: ECG before and after QT drug

name: Digoxin Level Interpretation
whenToUse: When a serum digoxin level is available and clinical context (efficacy vs toxicity) is being reviewed.
whyUse: Modern HF targets favor lower levels (≈0.5–0.9 ng/mL); toxicity risk rises as levels increase, especially >2 ng/mL.

actions: Fab for life-threatening arrhythmia/K⁺/level per protocol

name: ATRIA Stroke Risk Score
whenToUse: Patients with non-valvular AF for stroke risk stratification (especially when comparing schemes).
whyUse: Includes renal function and proteinuria; age is weighted more heavily, with different points if prior stroke.

name: ABC Stroke Score (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Educational stratification of AF stroke risk using age, prior stroke, and biomarker category proxies.
whyUse: Full ABC-stroke uses continuous NT-proBNP and hs-Tn with coefficients; this version teaches the domains with point bands.

actions: Do not rely on this simplified score alone for OAC decisions

name: ABC Bleeding Score (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Educational bleeding-risk discussion in AF on anticoagulation using age, prior bleed, and biomarker proxies.
whyUse: Full ABC-bleed uses GDF-15, hs-Tn, and hemoglobin with continuous coefficients; this teaches the concept with categories.

name: ACEF Score
whenToUse: Patients evaluated for cardiac surgery when a simple mortality risk index is desired.
whyUse: Parsimonious score with discrimination comparable to more complex models in some surgical series.

name: EuroSCORE II (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Teaching major EuroSCORE II risk factors only. Do not use for formal operative risk reporting.
whyUse: Highlights key clinical domains that drive cardiac surgical risk while clearly labeled as incomplete.

name: Mehran Contrast Nephropathy Risk Score
whenToUse: Patients undergoing PCI / contrast exposure when estimating CIN and dialysis risk.
whyUse: Widely used validated score for contrast-induced nephropathy risk stratification.

name: Forrester Hemodynamic Classification
whenToUse: When CI and PCWP (or clinical surrogates) are available in acute HF/MI shock phenotyping.
whyUse: Classic 2×2 profile that guides diuretics, inotropes, and vasodilators.

name: LDL-C (Sampson / NIH Equation)
whenToUse: Calculated LDL when TG are moderately elevated (up to ~800 mg/dL) or LDL is low.
whyUse: Outperforms Friedewald at low LDL and higher TG; usable when Friedewald is invalid.

nextSteps.condition: Elevated LDL or high ASCVD risk
actions: Statin intensity per AHA/ACC or ESC
Evaluate for secondary causes of hyperTG

name: LDL-C (Martin/Hopkins)
whenToUse: Calculated LDL with better accuracy than Friedewald at low LDL or higher TG (typically TG <400 mg/dL).
whyUse: AHA-supported alternative; factor varies with TG and non-HDL rather than fixed /5.

name: Non-HDL Cholesterol
whenToUse: Lipid risk assessment, especially when TG elevated or as a secondary treatment target.
whyUse: Includes LDL, VLDL, IDL, and remnant cholesterol; less dependent on fasting than calculated LDL.

actions: Add ezetimibe/PCSK9i if very high risk and not at goal

name: LDL / Non-HDL Goal Helper (ASCVD Risk Tier)
whenToUse: Setting lipid targets after risk stratification.
whyUse: Quick bedside reminder of intensity of LDL lowering by risk tier (AHA/ACC and ESC-style).

nextSteps.condition: Not at goal on max statin
actions: Consider PCSK9 inhibitor / bempedoic acid per indication

name: Triglyceride-Glucose Index (TyG)
whenToUse: Bedside estimate of insulin resistance from fasting TG and glucose.
whyUse: Simple, no insulin assay required; associated with metabolic syndrome and CV risk in studies.

name: HOMA-B (β-Cell Function)
whenToUse: Research or clinical estimate of β-cell function with fasting labs.
whyUse: Complements HOMA-IR; lower HOMA-B suggests reduced insulin secretion capacity.

name: QUICKI (Insulin Sensitivity)
whenToUse: Estimate insulin sensitivity without clamp study.
whyUse: Simple log-based index; correlates with clamp-derived insulin sensitivity.

actions: Screen for metabolic syndrome and T2DM

name: HbA1c % ↔ IFCC (mmol/mol)
whenToUse: Lab reports using different A1c unit systems.
whyUse: NGSP % (common in US) vs IFCC mmol/mol (common internationally).

name: Glucose Unit Conversion (mg/dL ↔ mmol/L)
whenToUse: Interpreting labs reported in different unit systems.
whyUse: US labs typically use mg/dL; many countries use mmol/L.

actions: Interpret in clinical context (fasting vs random)
Confirm with A1c / OGTT as appropriate

name: Creatinine Unit Conversion (mg/dL ↔ µmol/L)
whenToUse: Labs reported in different creatinine units.
whyUse: US often mg/dL; SI units µmol/L elsewhere.

name: Bilirubin Unit Conversion (mg/dL ↔ µmol/L)
whenToUse: Interpreting bilirubin across unit systems.
whyUse: Common conversion in hepatology and neonatology contexts.

name: Calcium Unit Conversion (mg/dL ↔ mmol/L)
whenToUse: Labs reported in different calcium units.
whyUse: US typically mg/dL; SI mmol/L.

actions: Prefer ionized Ca if critically ill
Correct for albumin if total Ca only
Check PTH, Mg, vitamin D as indicated

name: Calcium-Phosphate Product
whenToUse: CKD mineral-bone disorder monitoring.
whyUse: Historically used threshold for ectopic calcification risk; still a quick composite marker.

name: Fractional Excretion of Potassium (FEK)
whenToUse: Hypokalemia workup (renal vs extrarenal losses) and selected hyperkalemia contexts.
whyUse: Low FEK suggests appropriate renal K conservation; high FEK suggests renal K wasting (context-dependent).

actions: Consider renovascular / mineralocorticoid workup if HTN

name: Urine Osmolal Gap (UOG)
whenToUse: Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis: diarrhea vs RTA differential.
whyUse: High UOG suggests robust NH₄⁺ excretion (extrarenal HCO₃ loss); low UOG suggests impaired renal acidification (RTA).

actions: Check K, urine pH, aldosterone axis

name: Henderson-Hasselbalch (pH from HCO₃ & PCO₂)
whenToUse: Cross-check ABG/VBG consistency or estimate pH from electrolytes + PCO₂.
whyUse: Core acid-base relationship between pH, PCO₂, and HCO₃⁻.

actions: Suspect lab error or extreme temperature/abnormal proteins

name: Albumin-Corrected Anion Gap
whenToUse: Metabolic acidosis workup with low albumin (ICU, cirrhosis, nephrosis).
whyUse: Hypoalbuminemia lowers observed AG and can mask a high-AG process.

name: Delta Ratio (ΔAG / ΔHCO₃)
whenToUse: High anion gap metabolic acidosis to detect concurrent NAGMA or metabolic alkalosis.
whyUse: Pure HAGMA should drop HCO₃ roughly with the rise in AG; deviations suggest a second process.

actions: Seek hidden metabolic alkalosis (vomiting, diuretics, volume contraction)

name: Simplified Strong Ion Difference (SID)
whenToUse: Stewart-style acid-base teaching or complex ICU acid-base interpretation adjunct.
whyUse: Reduced SID (e.g., hyperchloremia) associates with metabolic acidosis; elevated SID with alkalosis.

name: Free Water Clearance (Cₕ₂ₒ)
whenToUse: Hyponatremia / concentrating-diluting ability assessment with timed urine collection.
whyUse: Positive CH₂O = net free water excretion (dilute urine); negative = free water reabsorption (concentrated urine).

actions: Fluid restriction or saline per diagnosis
Seek DI if polyuria with low Uosm

name: Osmolar Clearance (Cₒₛₘ)
whenToUse: With free water clearance calculations and polyuria workups.
whyUse: Separates osmotic diuresis (high Cosm) from water diuresis (high V with low Uosm).

nextSteps.condition: Polyuria + low Uosm / low Cosm share
actions: Water deprivation / desmopressin testing pathway for DI

name: Creatinine Clearance (Timed Collection)
whenToUse: When measured clearance is needed (extremes of muscle mass, amputations, pregnancy, drug dosing uncertainty).
whyUse: Gold-standard bedside clearance formula before (or when) nuclear GFR unavailable.

name: HIT-6 Headache Impact Test
whenToUse: Quantify functional impact of headache/migraine in clinic or research follow-up.
whyUse: Brief, validated patient-reported impact score that tracks treatment response.

actions: Consider neurology or headache clinic referral
Neuroimaging / urgent workup if secondary headache suspected

name: MIDAS Migraine Disability Assessment
whenToUse: Baseline and follow-up disability from migraine over the prior 3 months.
whyUse: Simple day-count disability grade used in guidelines and trials to stratify care intensity.

actions: Limit simple/combo analgesics to avoid MOH
Consider CGRP pathway agents / specialty clinic

name: ICHD Migraine Without Aura Helper
whenToUse: Structured review of migraine without aura criteria during headache evaluation.
whyUse: Makes ICHD-3 criterion A–E explicit so documentation and diagnosis are consistent.

actions: Offer prevention if ≥4 headache days/month or significant disability
Still exclude red flags for secondary headache
Consider probable migraine, TTH, TAC, or secondary headache

name: Status Epilepticus Time Thresholds
whenToUse: Suspected prolonged seizure to apply operational SE time points and urgency of treatment.
whyUse: ILAE 2015 operational definition uses seizure-type-specific t1/t2 thresholds for early treatment and injury risk.

name: AED Therapeutic Level Interpreter
whenToUse: When an AED serum level is available and clinical correlation (efficacy/toxicity) is needed.
whyUse: Quick reference ranges for common ASMs; emphasizes treat-the-patient, not only the number.

actions: Consider dialysis only in extreme cases per toxicology

name: Estimated Free Phenytoin
whenToUse: Total phenytoin available with abnormal albumin (or ESRD) when free assay is delayed/unavailable.
whyUse: Free phenytoin drives effect/toxicity; estimation approximates free concentration from total + albumin.

name: UPDRS Motor (Simplified Bands)
whenToUse: After MDS-UPDRS Part III motor exam to communicate severity bands (not a full UPDRS form).
whyUse: Part III is the core motor severity metric in PD care and trials; bands aid counseling and treatment intensity.

actions: Consider advanced therapies if fluctuations/dyskinesia disabling

name: Hoehn and Yahr Stage
whenToUse: Global PD staging for communication, research strata, and rough disability overview.
whyUse: Universal PD stage language; complements UPDRS for functional distribution of disease.

actions: Consider advanced therapies if motor complications

name: EDSS (Simplified Select)
whenToUse: Document approximate EDSS band when full neurostatus scoring is already known or roughly staged.
whyUse: EDSS is the standard MS disability metric for care and trials; simplified entry aids quick interpretation.

name: DN4 Neuropathic Pain Score
whenToUse: Differentiate neuropathic from non-neuropathic pain in clinic.
whyUse: Brief validated screen combining symptoms and sensory signs; cutoff ≥4.

actions: Avoid relying solely on opioids for neuropathic pain

name: SLUMS Cognitive Score
whenToUse: Interpret an already-administered SLUMS total for MCI vs dementia ranges.
whyUse: Free, sensitive cognitive screen with education-specific cutoffs used widely in VA/geriatrics.

name: Clock Drawing Score (0–5)
whenToUse: Quick visuospatial/executive cognitive screen interpretation after clock drawing.
whyUse: Fast bedside screen sensitive to dementia and executive dysfunction; pairs with other screens.

name: MADRS Depression Score
whenToUse: Clinician-rated depression severity monitoring (enter total after MADRS administration).
whyUse: Sensitive to change in antidepressant trials; standard severity bands for treatment response.

name: HAM-D Depression Score
whenToUse: Interpret clinician-administered HAM-D/HDRS total for severity monitoring.
whyUse: Classic depression severity scale in research and specialty care.

name: HAM-A Anxiety Score
whenToUse: Clinician-rated anxiety severity after HAM-A administration.
whyUse: Classic anxiety severity scale for monitoring treatment response.

actions: Assess for panic, GAD, PTSD, substance use

name: Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI)
whenToUse: Interpret patient-completed BAI total for anxiety symptom severity.
whyUse: Common self-report anxiety severity measure emphasizing somatic symptoms.

name: Beck Depression Inventory-II
whenToUse: Interpret patient-completed BDI-II for depressive symptom severity.
whyUse: Standard self-report depression severity scale aligned with DSM symptom constructs.

name: Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS)
whenToUse: Clinician-rated mania severity after YMRS administration (enter total).
whyUse: Standard mania severity outcome in bipolar research and inpatient monitoring.

name: PANSS Total (Simplified Bands)
whenToUse: After full PANSS administration, interpret total score severity bands.
whyUse: PANSS total is a common global psychosis severity metric in research and specialty care.

actions: Adherence and plasma level if available

name: AUDIT (Full 10-Item)
whenToUse: Comprehensive alcohol misuse screening when AUDIT-C is positive or full risk stratification needed.
whyUse: WHO standard screen for hazardous, harmful, and dependent drinking patterns.

name: DAST-10 Drug Abuse Screening
whenToUse: Screen for problems related to drug use (not alcohol) in primary care, ED, and behavioral health.
whyUse: Brief validated severity screen guiding brief intervention vs specialty referral.

name: CAGE-AID Questionnaire
whenToUse: Ultra-brief combined alcohol and drug problem screening in primary care and ED.
whyUse: Extends classic CAGE to substances other than alcohol with the same four stems.

name: ASRS-v1.1 Adult ADHD Screen (Part A)
whenToUse: Adult ADHD screening in primary care or psychiatry intake.
whyUse: WHO/Harvard ASRS Part A is a validated 6-item screen; ≥4 shaded responses = positive.

actions: Screen mimics (sleep apnea, anxiety, depression, SUD)

name: Insomnia Severity Index (ISI)
whenToUse: Quantify insomnia severity and treatment response (enter total after ISI).
whyUse: Brief validated insomnia severity scale used in clinic and CBT-I research.

actions: Screen OSA (STOP-BANG), restless legs, mood/anxiety, substances
Cautious, short-term hypnotics only when appropriate

name: PCL-5 PTSD Checklist
whenToUse: Interpret PCL-5 total after patient completes the 20-item DSM-5 PTSD checklist.
whyUse: Standard DSM-5-aligned PTSD severity and screening measure for monitoring and provisional detection.

actions: Trauma-focused psychotherapy (PE, CPT, EMDR per guidelines)
Screen depression, substance use, TBI history

name: ASTCT CRS Grade (CAR-T)
whenToUse: Fever or suspected CRS after CAR-T, bispecifics, or other T-cell engagers to assign ASTCT CRS grade.
whyUse: Standardizes severity for tocilizumab/steroids decisions and trial reporting; grade drives escalation of care.

name: ASTCT ICANS Grade
whenToUse: Altered mental status, aphasia, seizures, or other neurotoxicity after CAR-T / immune effector cell therapy.
whyUse: Standard ICANS grade guides steroids, imaging, EEG, and ICU care independent of CRS grade.

name: CTCAE Neutropenia Grade
whenToUse: Grading chemo/immunotherapy-related neutropenia for toxicity reporting and G-CSF / delay decisions.
whyUse: Maps ANC to familiar grade 1–4 thresholds used in protocols and adverse event logs.

name: CTCAE Thrombocytopenia Grade
whenToUse: Grading treatment-related thrombocytopenia for hold parameters, transfusions, and AE reporting.
whyUse: Standard platelet grade thresholds used across solid tumor and heme protocols.

actions: Rule out HIT/ITP/ consumptive causes if unexpected

name: BSA Chemotherapy Dose (mg/m² × BSA)
whenToUse: Any BSA-based cytotoxic (e.g., R-CHOP components, other solid-tumor regimens) when converting mg/m² to mg.
whyUse: Reduces arithmetic error; optional Mosteller BSA from height/weight when BSA unknown.

actions: Document BSA method and dose reduction reason

name: Calvert Carboplatin Dose
whenToUse: Planning carboplatin when target AUC and GFR/CrCl are known (use measured GFR or Cockcroft–Gault/eGFR per protocol).
whyUse: Standard AUC-based dosing balances efficacy and thrombocytopenia risk better than mg/m² alone.

name: Okuda Staging (HCC)
whenToUse: Historical/educational staging of HCC when assessing tumor extent plus hepatic reserve.
whyUse: Simple four-factor stage that combines anatomy and function; largely superseded by BCLC but still referenced.

name: BCLC HCC Stage Helper
whenToUse: Treatment-oriented staging of hepatocellular carcinoma in multidisciplinary clinics.
whyUse: Links tumor burden, liver function, and PS to recommended therapy classes (ablation → transplant/resection → TACE → systemic → BSC).

name: CLIP Score (HCC)
whenToUse: Prognostic stratification of HCC using Child-Pugh, morphology, AFP, and portal thrombosis.
whyUse: Simple 0–6 score with survival gradients; complementary to BCLC/Okuda.

name: Milan Criteria (HCC Transplant)
whenToUse: Evaluating HCC patients for liver transplant candidacy by size/number limits.
whyUse: Within-Milan disease has excellent post-transplant survival; foundation of many allocation policies (with regional expansions).

name: RECIST 1.1 Response Category
whenToUse: Radiologic response assessment using sum of longest diameters of target lesions (and knowledge of new lesions).
whyUse: Standard trial/clinical language for CR/PR/SD/PD; educational calculator for % change mapping.

actions: Confirm with follow-up scan per protocol

name: ECOG Performance Status
whenToUse: Baseline and serial functional assessment for treatment eligibility, trials, and prognosis.
whyUse: Universal oncology language for fitness; many regimens require PS 0–1 or 0–2.

actions: Standard oncology pathways / trial eligibility review

name: Karnofsky Performance Status
whenToUse: Functional assessment when KPS is preferred (transplant, some solid tumors, palliative research).
whyUse: Finer granularity than ECOG; used in Motzer/IMDC (KPS <80) and transplant pathways.

actions: Note as adverse prognostic factor in relevant scores

name: Gail Model (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Teaching relative contribution of reproductive/family/biopsy factors to 5-year breast cancer risk discussion.
whyUse: Highlights who may warrant formal Gail/Tyrer-Cuzick calculation, genetic counseling, or preventive therapy discussion.

actions: Consider prevention options if formal risk high

name: NCCN Distress Thermometer
whenToUse: Routine psychosocial distress screening in cancer care (visit-based or pathway-based).
whyUse: Score ≥4 commonly triggers further evaluation and supportive care resources.

name: IMDC (Heng) Risk — Metastatic RCC
whenToUse: Treatment-naive or previously treated metastatic clear-cell RCC risk stratification for systemic therapy discussions.
whyUse: Guides prognosis and historically regimen intensity (favorable vs intermediate vs poor).

name: MSKCC Motzer Criteria — Metastatic RCC
whenToUse: Classic risk stratification of metastatic RCC (cytokine and early targeted-therapy era model).
whyUse: Five-factor model still cited; compare with IMDC (which adds neutrophils/platelets, drops LDH).

name: Hasenclever IPS (Advanced Hodgkin)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed advanced classical Hodgkin lymphoma risk stratification.
whyUse: Seven clinical/lab factors predict freedom from progression; informs intensity discussions historically.

actions: Follow modern HL guidelines (not IPS alone)

name: FLIPI (Follicular Lymphoma)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed follicular lymphoma risk stratification (FLIPI; consider FLIPI-2/m7-FLIPI for research).
whyUse: Five-factor score estimates overall survival risk groups and frames observation vs treatment discussions.

name: IPI (Aggressive NHL)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed aggressive NHL / DLBCL before or at start of immunochemotherapy.
whyUse: Classic five-factor OS model; foundation for R-IPI and CNS-IPI.

name: Pittsburgh Knee Rules
whenToUse: Acute knee injury from blunt trauma or fall (not twisting-only without fall).
whyUse: High sensitivity alternative/adjunct to Ottawa Knee Rules; mechanism-focused.

actions: Ortho follow-up if fracture or locked knee
Reassess if not improving or inability to bear weight develops

name: Ottawa Hip Rules
whenToUse: Adults with acute hip or groin pain after fall or blunt trauma.
whyUse: Supports selective imaging while retaining high sensitivity for hip fracture.

actions: If films negative but cannot walk: MRI or CT for occult fracture

name: Kocher Criteria (Pediatric Septic Hip)
whenToUse: Child with acute nontraumatic hip pain / limp / irritable hip evaluating septic arthritis vs transient synovitis.
whyUse: Stratifies urgency for urgent aspiration/OR vs observation.

actions: IV antibiotics after synovial fluid obtained if stable

name: Thompson Test (Achilles Rupture)
whenToUse: Sudden calf/heel pain, “pop,” or weakness with push-off after sport or trauma.
whyUse: Positive Thompson is highly suggestive of complete Achilles rupture.

actions: Non-weight-bearing / functional brace in plantar flexion per protocol

name: Salter-Harris Classification
whenToUse: Pediatric fractures involving or near the growth plate.
whyUse: Guides prognosis for growth disturbance and treatment urgency.

name: Gustilo-Anderson Open Fracture Classification
whenToUse: Any open fracture for communication, antibiotics, and surgical planning.
whyUse: Correlates with infection risk, soft-tissue coverage needs, and outcomes.

name: Mirels Score (Pathologic Fracture Risk)
whenToUse: Prophylactic fixation decisions for metastatic lesions in long bones.
whyUse: Standardized site/pain/lesion/size scoring for fracture risk counseling.

name: Garden Classification (Femoral Neck)
whenToUse: Adult femoral neck fracture characterization and surgical planning.
whyUse: Communicates displacement; guides ORIF vs arthroplasty decisions with age/comorbidity.

actions: Time-to-OR goals per institutional hip-fracture protocol
Urgent reduction and fixation to protect blood supply

name: Neer Classification (Proximal Humerus)
whenToUse: Proximal humerus fracture description using displaced “parts.”
whyUse: Standard language for displacement pattern and treatment discussion.

name: Weber Ankle Fracture Classification
whenToUse: Lateral malleolar / fibular fractures about the ankle.
whyUse: Quick communication of syndesmotic level and stability concerns.

actions: Ortho consult for ORIF ± syndesmotic fixation

name: PECARN Pediatric C-Spine Risk Helper
whenToUse: Children after blunt trauma when considering cervical spine imaging.
whyUse: Highlights factors associated with CSI to support imaging decisions (not a standalone clearance rule).

actions: Consider clinical clearance if age-appropriate and cooperative

name: Injury Severity Score (ISS)
whenToUse: Trauma registries, research, and severity stratification after AIS coding.
whyUse: Standard anatomic injury burden metric (major trauma often ISS >15).

name: New Injury Severity Score (NISS)
whenToUse: When multiple severe injuries share one body region (ISS may undercall severity).
whyUse: Often outperforms ISS for mortality prediction when several injuries cluster in one region.

name: TRISS Survival Probability
whenToUse: Trauma audit, research, and educational survival probability estimates.
whyUse: Combines physiology (RTS), anatomy (ISS), age, and blunt vs penetrating mechanism.

actions: Use for audit/QI, not sole clinical decision-making
Document RTS components and AIS/ISS coding carefully

name: ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS A–E)
whenToUse: Traumatic or nontraumatic spinal cord injury grading after ISNCSCI exam.
whyUse: Standard international language for completeness and prognosis framing.

name: Frankel Grade (Spinal Cord)
whenToUse: Historical/educational SCI severity grading or literature comparison with ASIA.
whyUse: Simple five-grade scale preceding modern ASIA Impairment Scale.

actions: Record ASIA IS + NLI when possible for modern standards

name: Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS)
whenToUse: Outcome assessment after traumatic brain injury or other severe brain insults.
whyUse: Simple, widely used endpoint in TBI research and follow-up clinics.

name: Glasgow Outcome Scale–Extended (GOS-E)
whenToUse: More granular functional outcome after TBI than classic 5-point GOS.
whyUse: Standard secondary endpoint in modern TBI trials and clinics.

name: Fagan Nomogram (Post-test Probability)
whenToUse: Educational bedside Bayes: how much a test result changes disease probability.
whyUse: Makes LR+ / LR− actionable as updated probabilities.

actions: Consider treating / confirming with definitive test
Reconsider diagnosis if clinical suspicion remains high (bad prior or imperfect LR)

name: Likelihood Ratios from Sens/Spec
whenToUse: When a paper reports sens/spec and you need LR+ and LR− for Bayes updating.
whyUse: LRs transfer more cleanly across prevalence than PPV/NPV.

actions: Apply Fagan nomogram with clinical pre-test probability
Avoid using PPV alone without prevalence context

name: IDSA/ATS Severe CAP Criteria
whenToUse: Adults with CAP when deciding need for ICU or higher-level monitoring.
whyUse: IDSA/ATS 2007 defines severe CAP as ≥1 major or ≥3 minor criteria to guide ICU admission.

actions: Strongly consider ICU or high-dependency unit

name: SCAP Score (Severe CAP)
whenToUse: Adults with CAP to identify severe disease and ICU-level risk.
whyUse: Point-based alternative/complement to IDSA/ATS criteria with validated mortality prediction.

name: Hall Criteria (IV → Oral Switch, Pneumonia)
whenToUse: Hospitalized pneumonia patients on IV antibiotics being considered for oral step-down.
whyUse: Early switch when clinically stable shortens LOS without harming outcomes when criteria are met.

actions: Plan discharge if social support adequate

name: MuLBSTA Score (Viral Pneumonia)
whenToUse: Adults with confirmed or suspected viral pneumonia for early mortality risk stratification.
whyUse: Simple bedside/lab score derived for viral pneumonia outcomes including influenza.

name: ISARIC 4C Mortality Score (COVID-19)
whenToUse: Adults hospitalized with COVID-19 (or similar ILI pathways using 4C components).
whyUse: Validated multivariable mortality model using age, sex, comorbidities, vitals, and labs.

actions: Standard ward/outpatient pathway per local policy
Oxygen / steroids / antivirals per contemporary guidelines

name: Murray Lung Injury Score (Simplified)
whenToUse: Intubated patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure to grade lung injury.
whyUse: Classic composite severity score; >2.5 historically associated with severe lung injury/ARDS.

actions: Consider prone positioning if severe hypoxemia

name: Oxygenation Index (OI)
whenToUse: Mechanically ventilated patients when grading oxygenation failure (neonatal and adult critical care).
whyUse: Integrates FiO₂ and mean airway pressure with PaO₂; used in ECMO candidacy discussions (context-specific cutoffs).

actions: Specialty ECMO consult per local criteria

name: Bohr Dead Space Fraction (VD/VT)
whenToUse: When mixed-expired CO₂ (or equivalent) and arterial PCO₂ are available to estimate dead space.
whyUse: Elevated VD/VT indicates wasted ventilation (PE, COPD, low output, over-ventilation of dead space).

actions: Avoid excessive minute ventilation without addressing cause

name: Age-Expected PaO₂ (Room Air)
whenToUse: Interpreting room-air ABG oxygenation relative to age-expected normal.
whyUse: PaO₂ declines with age; absolute cutoffs misclassify older adults without age adjustment.

nextSteps.condition: PaO₂ much below expected on room air
actions: Evaluate for V/Q mismatch, shunt, hypoventilation
Consider imaging and ABG full panel

name: IMPROVE VTE Risk Score
whenToUse: Acutely ill medical inpatients when assessing need for pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis.
whyUse: Validated score identifying elevated VTE risk; often paired with IMPROVE bleed for net benefit.

actions: LMWH/UFH prophylaxis unless bleeding risk high
Avoid unnecessary prophylaxis if low risk and high bleed risk

name: Original Geneva Score (PE)
whenToUse: Suspected PE when original Geneva variables (including gases/CXR) are available.
whyUse: Predecessor to revised Geneva; still educationally useful. Revised Geneva is more practical at bedside without ABG.

actions: Do not rely on D-dimer alone

name: Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI)
whenToUse: Risk adjustment, prognosis discussions, research, and frailty/comorbidity burden estimates.
whyUse: Most widely used comorbidity index; correlates with survival and resource use.

name: SAPS II (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Teaching/approximate ICU severity when full SAPS II calculator is unavailable.
whyUse: SAPS II is a classic admission severity score; this version captures major drivers only.

actions: Use formal SAPS II/APACHE software for benchmarking

name: LODS Score (Simplified)
whenToUse: ICU patients for educational multi-organ dysfunction scoring.
whyUse: LODS estimates mortality from neurologic, CV, renal, pulmonary, hematologic, and hepatic dysfunction.

name: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score (Marshall)
whenToUse: ICU patients to quantify multi-organ dysfunction severity over time.
whyUse: Simple daily score correlating with ICU mortality; useful for serial tracking.

actions: Identify and reverse drivers of organ failure

name: C. difficile Infection Severity (IDSA-style)
whenToUse: Adults with confirmed or probable C. difficile infection to guide therapy intensity.
whyUse: Severity drives antibiotic choice and need for surgical/ICU consultation.

name: Sepsis-3 Septic Shock Helper
whenToUse: Patients with suspected infection and circulatory failure to apply Sepsis-3 septic shock criteria.
whyUse: Standardizes recognition of septic shock with substantially higher mortality than sepsis alone.

name: Procalcitonin Antibiotic Guidance Bands
whenToUse: Adults with lower respiratory infection or sepsis pathways using PCT algorithms (not a stand-alone diagnosis).
whyUse: PCT algorithms can safely reduce antibiotic exposure when combined with clinical judgment.

actions: Cultures before abx if no delay

name: TST Interpretation by Risk Group
whenToUse: Interpreting TST induration in mm according to CDC risk-stratified cut points.
whyUse: Prevents under-calling LTBI in high-risk patients and over-calling in low-risk persons.

name: DRIP Score (Drug-Resistant Pneumonia)
whenToUse: Adults with pneumonia when deciding need for extended-spectrum / dual MRSA-Pseudomonas coverage.
whyUse: Improves on HCAP criteria by weighting major and minor risk factors for drug-resistant pathogens.

actions: Cultures and nasal MRSA PCR if used locally

name: SCAI Cardiogenic Shock Stages
whenToUse: Patients with or at risk for cardiogenic shock (AMI, decompensated HF, post-arrest) to stage severity.
whyUse: Standardized language for shock trajectory; guides monitoring, vasoactives, MCS, and team activation.

name: INTERMACS Patient Profile
whenToUse: Advanced HF evaluation for durable MCS, transplant listing discussions, or acuity communication.
whyUse: Profiles correlate with outcomes after LVAD/transplant and standardize “how sick” language.

name: CardShock Risk Score
whenToUse: Adults with cardiogenic shock to estimate in-hospital mortality risk strata.
whyUse: Simple 7-variable score from a prospective European CS cohort; bedside applicable.

name: CRUSADE Bleeding Risk Score
whenToUse: NSTE-ACS patients when balancing ischemic vs bleeding risk for antithrombotic intensity.
whyUse: Widely cited bleeding risk model from the CRUSADE registry using admission variables.

name: DAPT Score
whenToUse: After coronary stenting when deciding whether to extend DAPT beyond 12 months (selected patients).
whyUse: Score ≥2 identifies patients more likely to benefit from prolonged DAPT; <2 favors standard duration.

actions: Discuss extended DAPT if low bleed risk
Focus on lifestyle and LDL therapy

name: PRECISE-DAPT (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Educational estimate of out-of-hospital bleeding risk to inform DAPT duration after coronary stenting.
whyUse: Highlights major PRECISE-DAPT predictors; full nomogram is preferred for precise cutoffs (e.g. ≥25).

name: HCM Risk-SCD (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Adults with HCM when framing SCD risk factors before using the official HCM Risk-SCD model or AHA pathway.
