whyUse: Counts major ESC-model inputs and classic risk markers for structured counseling; full 5-year % needs official tool.

name: Brugada ECG Pattern Helper
whenToUse: When ECG suggests Brugada pattern (rSR′ and STE in right precordial leads) for pattern typing.
whyUse: Type 1 is diagnostic; type 2 needs conversion/provocation context and clinical correlation.

name: Wellens Syndrome Helper
whenToUse: Chest pain patients with biphasic or deeply inverted precordial T waves after pain resolves.
whyUse: Recognizing Wellens pattern prompts urgent angiography rather than stress testing.

name: Smith-Modified Sgarbossa Criteria
whenToUse: Suspected occlusion MI with LBBB or ventricular paced rhythm when original Sgarbossa is negative/indeterminate.
whyUse: Proportional discordance improves sensitivity vs the fixed ≥5 mm discordant STE rule.

name: Right Heart Strain Flags (PE Helper)
whenToUse: Confirmed or suspected PE when cataloguing RV strain markers for severity discussion.
whyUse: Organizes ECG/echo strain findings that influence intermediate-high vs intermediate-low PE risk classification.

actions: Outpatient pathways only if Hestia/sPESI allow

name: BOVA Score (PE Severity)
whenToUse: Normotensive patients with confirmed acute PE for complication risk staging.
whyUse: Simple 0–7 point score (SBP, HR, RV dysfunction, troponin) with stage I–III risk bands.

actions: Often ward or selected outpatient if other rules allow

name: LV Mass (ASE Cube Formula)
whenToUse: Educational estimate of LV mass from IVSd, LVIDd, and PWT linear measurements.
whyUse: Quantifies LVH beyond voltage criteria; index to BSA for sex-specific reference ranges.

actions: Evaluate athlete’s heart vs pathologic LVH if relevant

name: Metabolic Syndrome (NCEP ATP III)
whenToUse: Adults undergoing cardiometabolic risk assessment in clinic or prevention visits.
whyUse: Simple binary diagnosis that identifies high residual ASCVD/diabetes risk clustering.

name: SCORE2 (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Adults 40–69 without prior ASCVD for educational European primary-prevention risk discussion.
whyUse: Mirrors SCORE2 inputs; full chart/algorithm needed for precise regional percentages.

name: Reynolds Risk Score (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Primary prevention adults when hsCRP and parental MI history are available (educational).
whyUse: Incorporates inflammation (hsCRP) and family history beyond traditional Framingham factors.

name: MESA CAC Score Helper
whenToUse: Primary prevention when a CAC Agatston score is available and age/sex known.
whyUse: Absolute CAC and rough percentile bands refine statin/aspirin discussions beyond risk estimators alone.

actions: Consider deferring statin if otherwise intermediate risk

name: Coronary Calcium Agatston Categories
whenToUse: When an Agatston CAC score is reported and absolute category interpretation is needed.
whyUse: Standard absolute cut-points used in reports and prevention pathways.

name: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI)
whenToUse: Suspected PAD, atypical leg symptoms, or CV risk stratification with Doppler SBP measurements.
whyUse: First-line noninvasive test for lower-extremity PAD diagnosis and severity.

name: Constans Score (Upper Extremity DVT)
whenToUse: Suspected upper-extremity DVT (arm swelling/pain ± catheter or pacemaker lead).
whyUse: Simple 4-item rule to stratify UEDVT pretest probability before ultrasound.

actions: Hold catheter decisions until imaging when feasible

name: Ottawa Score (Cancer-Associated VTE Recurrence)
whenToUse: Patients with cancer-associated VTE when estimating recurrence risk on anticoagulation.
whyUse: Identifies lower vs higher recurrence risk strata that may inform secondary prevention intensity/duration discussions.

actions: Lower threshold for investigating breakthrough symptoms

name: HERDOO2 Rule (Women, VTE Duration)
whenToUse: Women with unprovoked VTE after completing 5–12 months of anticoagulation when considering discontinuation.
whyUse: 0–1 HERDOO2 points ≈ low recurrence risk suitable for stopping in management studies; ≥2 continue.

name: Rome IV IBS Criteria Helper
whenToUse: Adults with chronic recurrent abdominal pain when considering IBS after appropriate red-flag evaluation.
whyUse: Structures the Rome IV definition (≥1 day/week pain for 3 months + ≥2 of 3 stool-related criteria; onset ≥6 months).

actions: Subtype-directed therapy (fiber, osmotic laxatives, antidiarrheals, neuromodulators)
Consider celiac serology / age-appropriate colonoscopy per guidelines
Broader differential (IBD, bile acid diarrhea, SIBO, endometriosis, etc.)

name: Bristol Stool Scale
whenToUse: Characterizing bowel habit in constipation, diarrhea, IBS subtyping, or patient education.
whyUse: Standard visual scale correlating form with colonic transit; improves history quality.

actions: Use for IBS subtyping if applicable

name: ABC Score (Upper GI Bleed)
whenToUse: Adults with acute upper GI bleeding for early mortality risk stratification alongside GBS/AIMS65/Rockall.
whyUse: Bedside ABC-style variables capture age, labs, mental status, and major comorbidity burden.

actions: Risk-stratify with GBS for intervention need
PPI ± vasoactive agents if variceal suspected

name: Oakland Score (Lower GI Bleed)
whenToUse: Adults with acute lower GI bleeding being considered for safe discharge vs admission.
whyUse: Oakland ≤8 often used as a low-risk threshold for safe discharge pathways in validated cohorts.

actions: Outpatient pathway if local protocol allows

name: SBO Strangulation Risk Features
whenToUse: Adhesive or other SBO when estimating risk of ischemia/strangulation needing urgent surgery.
whyUse: No single finding is definitive; accumulating systemic and peritoneal signs raise concern for strangulation.

actions: Early OR if fails nonop trial

name: CTSI (Balthazar) Pancreatitis
whenToUse: Contrast-enhanced CT in acute pancreatitis when grading morphologic severity.
whyUse: Combines pancreatic/peripancreatic inflammation grade with extent of necrosis; correlates with complications.

actions: Avoid early necrosectomy; step-up if infected necrosis

name: Modified Marshall Organ Failure (Pancreatitis)
whenToUse: Grading organ failure in acute pancreatitis per revised Atlanta classification.
whyUse: Organ failure (score ≥2 in any system) defines moderately severe/severe pancreatitis and drives ICU decisions.

name: Mannheim Peritonitis Index (Simplified)
whenToUse: Secondary peritonitis / intra-abdominal sepsis risk stratification perioperatively.
whyUse: Weighted clinical factors estimate mortality risk and support ICU triage decisions.

actions: Re-laparotomy on demand vs planned per strategy

name: Boey Score (Perforated Peptic Ulcer)
whenToUse: Patients with perforated peptic ulcer for perioperative mortality risk.
whyUse: Simple 0–3 score from medical illness, shock, and delayed presentation.

actions: Urgent surgical repair / selected nonop in contained cases

name: POSSUM Surgical Risk (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Teaching / rough physiologic burden estimate before major surgery (not a validated full POSSUM calculator).
whyUse: Highlights key physiologic domains used in POSSUM without claiming precise mortality percentages.

actions: Use institutional risk calculator for consent

name: Surgical Risk Helper (ACS-NSQIP style educational)
whenToUse: Quick teaching frame for relative perioperative risk before major surgery.
whyUse: Surfaces dominant predictors used in modern surgical risk models without claiming NSQIP accuracy.

name: ASA Physical Status Classification
whenToUse: Preoperative assessment and anesthesia documentation of systemic disease severity.
whyUse: Universal language for comorbidity burden; correlates with perioperative risk (not a standalone risk calculator).

name: Apfel PONV Risk Score
whenToUse: Adults before surgery to guide PONV prophylaxis intensity.
whyUse: Four binary predictors; risk rises ~20% per point — informs multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis.

name: Aldrete Post-Anesthesia Recovery Score
whenToUse: Post-anesthesia care unit readiness for discharge to ward or phase II.
whyUse: Standardized 0–10 recovery score; many units require ≥9 (with no zeros) before discharge.

actions: Discharge to ward/phase II per protocol

name: HEAVEN Difficult Airway Criteria
whenToUse: Before emergency RSI / intubation to anticipate difficulty and prepare backups.
whyUse: Mnemonic captures hypoxemia, body habitus extremes, anatomic disruption, contaminants, exsanguination, and neck issues.

actions: Standard RSI prep with backup plan

name: Cormack–Lehane Grade
whenToUse: Documenting glottic view during laryngoscopy and communicating difficulty.
whyUse: Universal grading of laryngeal exposure; higher grades predict harder intubation and need for adjuncts.

name: MACOCHA Score (ICU Intubation Difficulty)
whenToUse: Before intubation of critically ill adults in ICU/ED-ICU settings.
whyUse: Identifies high-risk ICU intubations (score ≥3) to trigger experienced operators and preparation.

actions: Standard ICU intubation bundle still applies

name: CATCH Rule (Pediatric Head CT)
whenToUse: Children with minor head injury (GCS 13–15) when deciding on CT — Canadian CATCH rule framework.
whyUse: High-sensitivity rule with high- and medium-risk features guiding imaging urgency.

name: CHALICE Rule (Pediatric Head Injury)
whenToUse: Children with head injury when applying CHALICE-style CT decision support (UK-derived).
whyUse: Lists history, examination, and mechanism features that historically triggered CT recommendation.

name: Dangerous Trauma Mechanism Helper
whenToUse: Blunt trauma evaluation when mechanism informs imaging, trauma activation, or decision rules.
whyUse: Standardizes which mechanisms elevate concern for major injury across C-spine, head, chest, and general trauma pathways.

name: ATLS Hemorrhagic Shock Class
whenToUse: Trauma or major hemorrhage to estimate blood-loss class and resuscitation intensity.
whyUse: Shared language for estimated % blood loss and expected vital-sign changes (educational — real patients vary).

name: ABC Score (Massive Transfusion)
whenToUse: Major trauma patients when deciding early activation of massive transfusion protocol.
whyUse: Four binary ED variables; score ≥2 predicts massive transfusion need with good balance of sensitivity/specificity.

name: MELD-XI Score
whenToUse: End-stage liver disease prognosis when INR is unreliable (warfarin, DOAC, DIC) or unavailable.
whyUse: Retains bilirubin and creatinine prognostic information without coagulation; educational alternative to full MELD/MELD-Na.

actions: Do not use alone for listing priority
Prefer MELD-XI or clinical judgment over INR-driven MELD

name: PELD Score
whenToUse: Children <12 years with chronic liver disease for prognosis / transplant prioritization context.
whyUse: Age-appropriate counterpart to MELD using bilirubin, INR, albumin, age <1 year, and growth failure.

name: UKELD Score
whenToUse: Adult chronic liver disease when estimating transplant benefit using UK-style labs (includes sodium).
whyUse: UK listing threshold historically UKELD ≥49; incorporates INR, creatinine, bilirubin, and sodium.

name: CLIF-C ACLF Score (Simplified)
whenToUse: Hospitalized cirrhosis with acute-on-chronic liver failure for mortality risk estimate.
whyUse: Prognostic score for ACLF severity; complements CLIF-OF/CLIF-SOFA organ grading.

name: CLIF-SOFA / CLIF-OF (Simplified Sum)
whenToUse: Bedside educational grading of organ dysfunction in decompensated cirrhosis / ACLF workup.
whyUse: Organ-failure count and severity define ACLF grades and feed CLIF-C ACLF.

name: ABIC Score (Alcoholic Hepatitis)
whenToUse: Confirmed or probable alcoholic hepatitis for risk stratification (complements Maddrey, GAHS, MELD).
whyUse: Continuous score with low/intermediate/high 90-day mortality strata.

name: AST/ALT Ratio (De Ritis)
whenToUse: Interpreting aminotransferase pattern in suspected alcoholic liver disease, cirrhosis, or mixed injury.
whyUse: Ratio >1 (especially >2) supports alcohol-related injury or advanced fibrosis; <1 common in viral/NAFLD hepatitis without cirrhosis.

name: SAAG (Serum-Ascites Albumin Gradient)
whenToUse: After diagnostic paracentesis when serum and ascites albumin are available.
whyUse: SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL indicates portal hypertension with high accuracy; guides differential and therapy.

name: Runyon Criteria (Secondary Peritonitis)
whenToUse: Ascitic infection when distinguishing SBP from secondary peritonitis needing source control.
whyUse: ≥2 chemical criteria raise concern for secondary peritonitis and prompt imaging/surgery.

name: HAPS (Harmless Acute Pancreatitis Score)
whenToUse: Early evaluation of acute pancreatitis to identify patients suitable for ward care.
whyUse: Absence of peritonitis signs, hemoconcentration, and renal failure predicts mild course with high NPV.

name: PNED Score (UGIB Mortality, Simplified)
whenToUse: Adults with nonvariceal upper GI bleeding for in-hospital mortality risk stratification.
whyUse: Includes clinical and post-endoscopy factors (rebleed, failed endoscopic therapy) beyond pure admission scores.

name: Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS)
whenToUse: Children with suspected appendicitis to structure probability and imaging decisions.
whyUse: Pediatric-specific alternative/complement to Alvarado; includes hop tenderness and neutrophilia.

name: Tokyo Guidelines Cholangitis Severity
whenToUse: Confirmed or suspected acute cholangitis after diagnosis criteria met (systemic inflammation + cholestasis + imaging).
whyUse: Grade guides urgency of biliary drainage and intensity of care.

name: Tokyo Guidelines Cholecystitis Severity
whenToUse: Acute cholecystitis once diagnostic criteria are met, to grade severity and plan intervention.
whyUse: Grade III organ dysfunction and Grade II local/inflammatory markers change operative risk and need for drainage.

actions: Surgical pathway per fitness and local inflammation

name: Determinant-Based Pancreatitis Severity
whenToUse: Acute pancreatitis when (peri)pancreatic necrosis and organ-failure duration are known or suspected.
whyUse: Separates sterile vs infected necrosis and transient vs persistent organ failure for prognosis and management intensity.

name: Mayo Natural History Model (PBC)
whenToUse: PBC prognosis discussions and transplant timing context (educational R score).
whyUse: Classic model using age, bilirubin, albumin, PT, and edema; higher R → worse survival.

name: Prague C & M (Barrett Esophagus)
whenToUse: Documenting Barrett esophagus extent at endoscopy for surveillance planning.
whyUse: Standardized C&M reporting improves communication and correlates with neoplastic risk burden.

name: Los Angeles Classification (Esophagitis)
whenToUse: Endoscopic grading of erosive esophagitis severity.
whyUse: Standardized grades guide GERD severity documentation, PPI intensity, and healing expectations.

actions: Screen for Barrett once healed if indicated

name: Baveno VI Criteria (Varices Screening)
whenToUse: Compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) when deciding need for screening EGD for varices needing treatment.
whyUse: LSM <20 kPa and platelets >150×10⁹/L identify patients at very low risk of varices needing treatment who can defer endoscopy.

name: HVPG Interpretation
whenToUse: Interpreting measured HVPG from hepatic vein catheterization.
whyUse: HVPG thresholds define CSPH, variceal bleeding risk, and treatment response targets.

name: Ascites PMN (SBP Diagnosis)
whenToUse: Diagnostic paracentesis in ascites — especially cirrhosis with symptoms, admission, or GI bleed.
whyUse: PMN ≥250/µL diagnoses SBP and warrants prompt antibiotics without waiting for culture.

name: Delta-MELD (ΔMELD)
whenToUse: Serial MELD scores in decompensated cirrhosis or waitlist monitoring.
whyUse: Rising MELD (positive ΔMELD) associates with higher mortality beyond static MELD alone.

actions: US Doppler for portal vein thrombus

name: FibroScan LSM → Fibrosis Stage (Approx)
whenToUse: Interpreting vibration-controlled transient elastography (FibroScan) LSM in chronic liver disease.
whyUse: Etiology-aware kPa cut-offs triage advanced fibrosis/cirrhosis risk for clinical pathways.

actions: Assume advanced disease until proven otherwise

name: Maddrey DF Unit Helper (PT vs INR)
whenToUse: When calculating Maddrey DF and labs report INR more readily than PT/control.
whyUse: Original DF uses PT in seconds vs control; INR-based shortcuts are imperfect and lab-dependent.

name: GerdQ Questionnaire
whenToUse: Primary care or GI clinic assessment of suspected GERD and monitoring symptom control.
whyUse: Structured 6-item score; ≥8 suggests GERD and may support empiric PPI trial in typical patients.

name: CKD-EPI 2021 Creatinine eGFR (Race-Free)
whenToUse: Adult CKD detection, staging, and monitoring using serum creatinine.
whyUse: NKF-ASN preferred race-free creatinine equation (Inker 2021).

name: CKD-EPI Cystatin C eGFR
whenToUse: When creatinine is unreliable (low muscle mass, amputation, extremes of diet) or to confirm eGFR.
whyUse: Cystatin C less dependent on muscle mass; useful confirmatory or alternative equation.

actions: Review muscle mass, diet, steroids, thyroid disease
Consider measured GFR if decisions hinge on value

name: KDIGO eGFR G Stage
whenToUse: Convert any eGFR/GFR value into KDIGO G category for documentation and risk framing.
whyUse: Standard CKD GFR categories used with albuminuria for prognosis.

actions: BP and metabolic bone/anemia screening as indicated

name: KDIGO CKD Heat Map (G × A Risk)
whenToUse: CKD risk stratification for monitoring frequency and referral urgency.
whyUse: Combined G and A categories predict progression and CV outcomes better than GFR alone.

name: RIFLE AKI Criteria
whenToUse: Staging AKI by creatinine/GFR change and/or urine output criteria.
whyUse: Foundational consensus AKI criteria preceding AKIN and KDIGO.

name: AKIN AKI Staging
whenToUse: Staging AKI with AKIN criteria (48-hour window for creatinine rise).
whyUse: Refined RIFLE; bridge to current KDIGO staging.

name: Renal Angina Index (Simplified)
whenToUse: Early risk stratification for AKI in at-risk hospitalized/ICU patients (educational adult adaptation).
whyUse: Concept of “renal angina” combines predisposition risk with early signs of injury (Cr change, fluid overload).

name: Furosemide Stress Test (FST)
whenToUse: Oliguric early AKI to assess tubular responsiveness and risk of progression (after euvolemia ensured).
whyUse: UO response after 1–1.5 mg/kg IV furosemide predicts progression and need for RRT better than many static markers.

actions: Match UOP with intake if needed

name: FENa on Diuretics + FeUrea
whenToUse: Oliguric AKI differential when patient has received diuretics.
whyUse: FENa rises after loops even if prerenal; FeUrea is preferred in that setting.

name: Electrolyte-Free Water Clearance (cEFWC)
whenToUse: Hyponatremia / free-water balance assessment using urine electrolytes and volume.
whyUse: Estimates whether kidneys are excreting or retaining electrolyte-free water.

actions: Fluid restriction or treat SIADH cause

name: Infusate ΔNa (Adrogué Table)
whenToUse: Planning IV fluid Na content effect for dysnatremia correction.
whyUse: Estimates ΔNa per 1 L of D5W, 0.45% NaCl, 0.9% NaCl, or 3% NaCl.

actions: DDAVP clamp strategy in selected high-risk hyponatremia

name: Estimated Potassium Deficit
whenToUse: Rough planning for K repletion in hypokalemia (not exact total-body K).
whyUse: Provides order-of-magnitude deficit; actual needs vary with ongoing losses and pH.

actions: IV K per institutional max rates

name: Chloride Deficit (Metabolic Alkalosis)
whenToUse: Chloride-depletion (saline-responsive) metabolic alkalosis volume/Cl repletion planning.
whyUse: Rough Cl deficit helps estimate NS volume needed when alkalosis is Cl-responsive.

actions: Stop or reduce loop/thiazide if possible

name: IV Potassium Rate Safety Check
whenToUse: Before/while ordering IV KCl to compare planned rate with usual safety ceilings.
whyUse: Rapid IV K risks arrhythmia; institutions set max rates and concentrations.

actions: Reduce rate or use central access

name: Ionized Calcium pH Correction
whenToUse: When iCa is measured at a non-physiologic pH and you want an approximate 7.40-normalized value.
whyUse: Acidemia increases iCa; alkalemia decreases iCa — correction aids interpretation.

actions: Replace Ca if symptomatic or severe

name: Phosphate Replacement Estimate
whenToUse: Planning repletion for hypophosphatemia (weight-based mmol estimates).
whyUse: Severity-stratified mmol/kg guidance commonly used in ICU protocols.

name: VExUS Score (Venous Congestion)
whenToUse: Bedside assessment of systemic venous congestion (heart failure, AKI, fluid intolerance).
whyUse: Integrates hepatic vein, portal vein, and intrarenal venous Doppler into a congestion grade.

name: IVC Collapsibility Index
whenToUse: Bedside ultrasound volume assessment (spontaneous breathing or controlled ventilation).
whyUse: CI% estimates RAP / fluid responsiveness when used with correct respiratory context.

name: Passive Leg Raise (PLR) Interpretation
whenToUse: Predict fluid responsiveness without committing to a fluid bolus.
whyUse: PLR reversibly mobilizes ~300 mL venous blood; SV/CO increase ≥10–15% predicts responders.

name: Pulse Pressure Variation (PPV)
whenToUse: Fully adapted patients on controlled ventilation to predict fluid responsiveness.
whyUse: Dynamic arterial waveform index; PPV >12–13% often predicts responders under valid conditions.

name: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure (CPP)
whenToUse: Neurocritical care when ICP (or surrogate) and MAP are available.
whyUse: Maintains estimate of net pressure driving cerebral blood flow; common goals ≥60 mmHg.

actions: Optimize MAP with fluids/vasopressors per protocol

name: Oxygen Delivery (DO₂)
whenToUse: Shock / high-risk perioperative care when CO and ABG/oximetry available.
whyUse: Quantifies bulk O₂ transport; low DO₂ may contribute to tissue hypoxia.

actions: Consider transfusion only per restrictive thresholds

name: New Ballard Score (Gestational Age)
whenToUse: Newborns when menstrual dating is uncertain and physical/neuromuscular maturity assessment is used.
whyUse: Standard bedside maturity score mapping total points to approximate weeks of gestation.

actions: Thermoregulation, glucose, respiratory support as indicated
Prefer earliest US dating when reliable
Reassess maturity if clinical picture discordant

name: Silverman-Anderson Respiratory Distress Score
whenToUse: Newborns with signs of respiratory distress to grade severity and trend response to support.
whyUse: Simple reproducible bedside score for upper/lower chest movement, xiphoid retraction, nares, and grunting.

name: Bedside PEWS (Pediatric Early Warning)
whenToUse: Hospitalized children for early recognition of clinical deterioration.
whyUse: Structures vital signs and work-of-breathing into an actionable early-warning total.

name: SNAPPE-II (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: NICU teaching on illness severity in the first 12 hours of life (not a substitute for full SNAPPE-II software).
whyUse: Illustrates how physiology + perinatal factors stratify neonatal mortality risk.

actions: Counsel family using local outcomes data
Do not rely solely on educational score

name: CRIB-II (Simplified Educational)
whenToUse: Teaching mortality risk stratification for infants ≤32 weeks at admission (educational).
whyUse: Highlights major CRIB-II predictors in a bedside-friendly form.

name: N-PASS (Pain / Agitation / Sedation) Simplified
whenToUse: NICU neonates for ongoing pain/agitation assessment or sedation depth monitoring.
whyUse: Combines behavioral and physiologic cues with sedation scoring (−2 to +2 style domains).

name: FLACC Pain Scale
whenToUse: Children who cannot self-report pain (typically 2 months–7 years, also nonverbal patients).
whyUse: Widely used observational scale for acute pain intensity.

name: Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale
whenToUse: Verbal children who can match faces to how they feel (often ≥3 years).
whyUse: Simple self-report tool validated across ages and cultures.

name: Neonatal Infant Pain Scale (NIPS)
whenToUse: Term and preterm neonates for procedural or postoperative pain assessment.
whyUse: Quick bedside behavioral score used widely in nurseries and NICUs.

name: AVPU Responsiveness Scale
whenToUse: Rapid assessment of responsiveness in emergency, prehospital, or ward deterioration.
whyUse: Faster than full GCS for triage; maps roughly to GCS bands.

name: Broselow Color Zone (Educational)
whenToUse: Pediatric emergencies when length-based tape or estimated weight guides drug/equipment sizing.
whyUse: Color zones reduce cognitive load for weight-based dosing during resuscitation.

actions: Use ideal body weight policies per institution when indicated

name: Pediatric Uncuffed ETT Size
whenToUse: Children ≥1–2 years when estimating oral ETT size for intubation (not neonates).
whyUse: Classic Cole formula for uncuffed tubes; cuffed tubes often ~0.5 mm smaller.

name: Pediatric Hypotension SBP Threshold (PALS-style)
whenToUse: Ill children when interpreting whether SBP is below age-based hypotension threshold.
whyUse: PALS defines hypotension cutoffs that differ markedly by age; adults thresholds mislead.

actions: Do not be reassured by “normal” BP alone

name: Holliday-Segar Daily Maintenance Fluids
whenToUse: Children needing maintenance IV fluids when calculating daily/hourly volume.
whyUse: Classic weight-based maintenance estimate used worldwide.

name: Pediatric KDIGO AKI Stage (Creatinine)
whenToUse: Children with rising creatinine when staging AKI severity.
whyUse: KDIGO stages guide monitoring intensity and nephrology involvement; same fold-change stages apply in pediatrics.

name: Pediatric Urine Output / Oliguria
whenToUse: Hospitalized children when assessing oliguria or AKI by urine volume.
whyUse: Weight-normalized UOP is more meaningful than absolute mL/h in pediatrics.

name: PECARN Blunt Abdominal Trauma (Simplified)
whenToUse: Children with blunt torso trauma when deciding need for abdominal CT.
whyUse: Identifies very low-risk children who may avoid CT radiation if no predictors present.

actions: Observation vs discharge with reliable follow-up

name: Bronchiolitis Clinical Severity Bands
whenToUse: Infants and young children with bronchiolitis for severity-based disposition and support.
whyUse: Structures work of breathing, feeding, and oxygen need into actionable severity bands.

name: Pediatric Asthma Exacerbation Severity
whenToUse: Children with acute asthma flare for severity-based treatment intensity.
whyUse: Aligns exam findings with stepwise acute asthma therapy and disposition.

name: Pediatric Asthma Score (PAS)
whenToUse: Pediatric ED/inpatient pathways that use PAS for escalation and discharge readiness.
whyUse: Standardized scoring used in many children’s hospital asthma pathways.

name: Philadelphia Criteria (Febrile Infant)
whenToUse: Febrile infants (classically 29–60 days) when applying Philadelphia low-risk criteria.
whyUse: Historical well-validated set of low-risk criteria including LP in the original pathway.

name: Boston Criteria (Febrile Infant)
whenToUse: Febrile infants (classically 28–89 days) when applying Boston low-risk laboratory criteria.
whyUse: Another classic low-risk rule set still referenced in teaching and comparisons.

actions: Follow local protocol (may differ from 1990s Boston strategy)

name: PECARN Febrile Infant Rule (Simplified Age Bands)
whenToUse: Febrile infants ≤60 days when applying PECARN prediction rules for invasive bacterial infection risk.
whyUse: Multicenter PECARN rules identify low-risk infants using UA, ANC, and PCT with age stratification.

actions: Do not use outpatient low-risk discharge

name: Incomplete Kawasaki Disease Lab Helper
whenToUse: Children with ≥5 days of fever and 2–3 clinical KD features when applying supplemental lab criteria.
whyUse: Incomplete KD needs lab + echo algorithm to avoid missed coronary risk.

name: WHO Dehydration Classification
whenToUse: Children with diarrhea/gastroenteritis when classifying dehydration for fluid plans.
whyUse: Global standard linking clinical signs to ORS vs IV rehydration strategy.

name: ORS Volume by Weight & Dehydration %
whenToUse: Calculating deficit replacement volume for oral rehydration.
whyUse: Deficit (mL) ≈ weight(kg) × % dehydration × 10; WHO Plan B uses ~75 mL/kg over 4 h for some dehydration.

name: Partogram Progress Alert (Educational)
whenToUse: Active labor teaching when comparing dilation progress to time expectations (not a full WHO partograph).
whyUse: Flags slower-than-expected progress for closer evaluation of power/passenger/passage.

actions: Confirm adequate MVUs ≥4 h (or ≥6 h oxytocin)
Shared decision on cesarean if true arrest

name: Gestational Hypertension Diagnostic Helper
whenToUse: New hypertension after 20 weeks without clear chronic HTN history.
whyUse: Gestational HTN vs preeclampsia drives monitoring intensity and delivery timing.

name: Carpenter-Coustan GDM Thresholds
whenToUse: After abnormal 1-hour glucose challenge when interpreting 3-hour 100-g OGTT by Carpenter-Coustan criteria.
whyUse: Common US diagnostic thresholds for GDM on 3-hour OGTT (2 or more elevations).

name: Umbilical Cord Gas Interpretation
whenToUse: After delivery when umbilical artery (or vein) blood gas results are available.
whyUse: pH and base deficit help classify severity of fetal acidemia and guide neonatal concern.

actions: Routine neonatal care with observation as indicated

name: Symphysis-Fundal Height vs Weeks
whenToUse: Antenatal visits after ~20–24 weeks when measuring SFH for growth surveillance.
whyUse: Simple screen: SFH (cm) roughly equals weeks ±2–3 cm; larger deviations prompt ultrasound.

name: Estimated Fetal Weight (Hadlock Simplified)
whenToUse: Interpreting ultrasound biometrics to estimate fetal weight (educational calculation).
whyUse: Hadlock formulas are widely used in obstetric ultrasound for EFW.

actions: Clinical pelvimetry / induction policies per local protocol

name: Toxic Alcohol Osmolar Gap Helper
whenToUse: Suspected toxic alcohol ingestion with measured and calculated osmolality ± known ethanol level.
whyUse: Elevated osmolar gap suggests unmeasured osmotically active solutes (alcohols, acetone, severe hyperlipidemia/proteins, mannitol).

nextSteps.condition: Elevated gap ± acidosis / visual symptoms / oxalate crystals

actions: Reassess if anion gap rises later

name: Estimated Methanol from Osmolar Gap
whenToUse: When methanol level is pending and residual osm gap is attributed to methanol.
whyUse: Rapid ballpark for severity while awaiting quantitative methanol.

name: Estimated Ethylene Glycol from Osmolar Gap
whenToUse: Suspected EG ingestion with residual osm gap while quantitative level pending.
whyUse: Provides bedside estimate of parent alcohol burden to support antidote/HD decisions with full clinical picture.

name: N-Acetylcysteine IV Dosing (21-hour)
whenToUse: Acetaminophen overdose when IV NAC is indicated (nomogram, unknown time, fulminant pathway, etc.).
whyUse: Standard three-bag protocol doses are weight-based; errors in bag preparation are common.

actions: Start without delay if criteria met
Consider extended NAC, HD discussion if very high levels/acidosis

name: Digoxin Immune Fab Vial Estimate
whenToUse: Life-threatening digoxin toxicity or planning Fab dosing with known level or ingested amount.
whyUse: Vial estimates guide pharmacy preparation; underdosing leaves free digoxin activity.

actions: Avoid calcium as “stone heart” dogma is debated — follow local tox guidance
Renal clearance of Fab-digoxin complex delayed in CKD

name: Salicylate Toxicity Severity Helper
whenToUse: Known or suspected salicylate poisoning with a quantitative level.
whyUse: Levels guide urgency, but chronic toxicity is severe at lower concentrations than acute.

name: Fomepizole Dosing
whenToUse: Confirmed or highly suspected methanol or ethylene glycol poisoning.
whyUse: ADH inhibition is time-critical; weight-based dosing and redosing with HD differ from standard q12h.

name: Naloxone Infusion Rate (Rule of Thumb)
whenToUse: Recurrent opioid respiratory depression after bolus naloxone, especially long-acting opioids.
whyUse: Provides a practical starting infusion when boluses must be repeated frequently.

name: Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria
whenToUse: Possible serotonin toxicity after serotonergic drugs (SSRI/SNRI, MAOI, tramadol, linezolid, MDMA, etc.).
whyUse: Hunter criteria are more sensitive/specific than older Sternbach criteria in validation cohorts.

actions: Avoid pure dopamine antagonists if SS likely

name: NMS Diagnostic Criteria Helper
whenToUse: Fever and rigidity in a patient on antipsychotics or after abrupt dopamine agonist withdrawal.
whyUse: Structures cardinal features (exposure, rigidity, hyperthermia, autonomic instability, CK/mental status).

name: Anticholinergic Toxidrome Checklist
whenToUse: Altered patient with possible anticholinergic overdose (antihistamines, TCAs, atropine, plants).
whyUse: Rapid toxidrome pattern recognition guides physostigmine consideration and differential.

name: Cholinergic Toxidrome (SLUDGE / DUMBBELS)
whenToUse: Suspected organophosphate, carbamate, nerve agent, or nicotine excess with secretory toxidrome.
whyUse: Early recognition drives atropine, pralidoxime (for OP), decontamination, and airway support.

name: Opioid Toxidrome Checklist
whenToUse: Suspected opioid intoxication with CNS and respiratory depression.
whyUse: The classic triad plus supporting features supports naloxone trial and monitoring plan.

actions: Avoid large boluses in dependent patients when possible

name: Pack-Years Smoking
whenToUse: Quantifying cumulative tobacco exposure for screening and risk discussion.
whyUse: Pack-years inform lung cancer screening eligibility and COPD risk framing.

name: Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence
whenToUse: Assessing physical nicotine dependence to guide cessation intensity.
whyUse: Higher scores predict withdrawal severity and benefit from more intensive pharmacotherapy.

name: Alcohol Content & Standard Drinks
whenToUse: Counseling on intake, documenting exposure, or estimating ethanol load.
whyUse: Volume × ABV is more accurate than “number of drinks” when pour sizes vary.

name: US Navy Body Fat Estimate
whenToUse: Quick anthropometric body-fat estimate when DEXA/BIA unavailable.
whyUse: Simple field method used by US military standards; better than BMI alone for composition.

name: Waist–Hip Ratio (WHR)
whenToUse: Assessing central adiposity and cardiometabolic risk beyond BMI.
whyUse: WHR captures fat distribution associated with CVD and metabolic disease risk.

name: ACR TI-RADS (Simplified Points)
whenToUse: Risk-stratifying thyroid nodules on ultrasound for FNA decisions.
whyUse: Standardizes lexicon and biopsy thresholds by TR level and size.

name: Bethesda Thyroid Cytology Interpreter
whenToUse: After thyroid FNA when a Bethesda category is reported.
whyUse: Standardizes implied malignancy risk and next-step framework (with 2017/2023 updates).

actions: Pre-op TSH, vocal cord assessment as indicated

name: Burch–Wartofsky Point Scale (Thyroid Storm)
whenToUse: Severe thyrotoxicosis when distinguishing uncomplicated thyrotoxicosis from thyroid storm.
whyUse: Points-based likelihood guides ICU-level multimodality therapy urgency.

name: Myxedema Coma Diagnostic Score (Simplified)
whenToUse: Suspected decompensated hypothyroidism / myxedema coma in a critically ill patient.
whyUse: Structures thermoregulatory, CNS, cardiovascular, GI, and metabolic features while labs pending.

actions: IV levothyroxine ± liothyronine per expert protocol

name: DASH Score (Recurrent VTE)
whenToUse: After completing short-term anticoagulation for unprovoked VTE when considering extended therapy vs stop.
whyUse: Integrates D-dimer, age, sex, and hormone-associated VTE into a simple recurrence risk score (Tosetto et al.).

actions: Shared decision to stop vs continue

name: Vienna Prediction Model (Simplified VTE Recurrence)
whenToUse: Educational risk discussion after unprovoked VTE when weighing extended anticoagulation (not a full nomogram substitute).
whyUse: Highlights the three core Vienna predictors — sex, VTE location, and D-dimer — used in the continuous model.

name: VTE-BLEED Score
whenToUse: Patients with VTE on (or starting) anticoagulation when assessing major bleed risk.
whyUse: Simple 6-factor score validated for major bleeding during stable anticoagulation after VTE.

actions: Revisit net benefit of extended therapy

name: RIETE Simplified Score (Acute PE Prognosis)
whenToUse: Confirmed acute PE for rapid prognostic stratification (adjunct to sPESI/PESI).
whyUse: Seven binary RIETE items map low vs higher mortality risk strata from the RIETE registry.

name: Necrotizing Fasciitis Clinical Likelihood Helper
whenToUse: Suspected cellulitis vs necrotizing soft tissue infection (NSTI) — clinical suspicion pathway.
whyUse: LRINEC is insensitive; pain out of proportion, rapid spread, and hard signs drive surgical exploration decisions.

name: FeverPAIN Score (Full)
whenToUse: Acute sore throat in primary care / ED for bacterial probability and antibiotic strategy.
whyUse: Predicts group A strep likelihood; supports no / delayed / immediate antibiotic strategies (UK NICE).

actions: Immediate Abx or confirm with test

name: Peritonsillar Abscess Clinical Likelihood
whenToUse: Severe sore throat with possible PTA — triage for ENT drainage vs medical therapy.
whyUse: Trismus, uvular deviation, and unilateral swelling best discriminate PTA clinically.

name: Epiglottitis Red Flags
whenToUse: Severe sore throat, odynophagia out of proportion, or stridor — especially if pharynx looks benign.
whyUse: Missed epiglottitis risks abrupt airway obstruction; exam and imaging choices must protect the airway.

name: Retropharyngeal Abscess Red Flags (Pediatric)
whenToUse: Febrile child with neck stiffness, limited extension, drooling, or ill appearance after URI.
whyUse: Early RPA can mimic meningitis or simple pharyngitis; delayed diagnosis risks airway and mediastinitis.

name: Bacterial Meningitis Score (Nigrovic)
whenToUse: Children with CSF pleocytosis when deciding bacterial vs aseptic meningitis risk (after LP, not neonates).
whyUse: Score of 0 identifies a very low-risk group that may avoid prolonged antibiotics in validated settings.

name: Pyelonephritis Admission Criteria Helper
whenToUse: Adults (and older adolescents) with acute pyelonephritis when deciding ED discharge vs admit.
whyUse: Structures IDSA-aligned reasons that usually favor hospitalization and IV therapy.

name: Zar Score (C. difficile Severity)
whenToUse: Adults with confirmed CDI when classifying mild vs severe disease for therapy intensity.
whyUse: Simple bedside/lab score; ≥2 points defines severe CDI in the original Zar study.

name: ATLAS Score (C. difficile)
whenToUse: Hospitalized adults with CDI for severity and outcome risk stratification.
whyUse: Multivariable 0–10 score correlating with cure rates and prognosis in CDI trials/cohorts.

name: Lyme Disease Pretest Probability Helper
whenToUse: Patients with possible Lyme (rash, monoarthritis, facial palsy, etc.) when deciding empiric therapy vs testing.
whyUse: Serology predictive value depends heavily on pretest probability; EM in endemic areas is often a clinical diagnosis.

name: Age-Adjusted D-Dimer Threshold
whenToUse: Outpatients with non-high pretest PE/DVT probability when using D-dimer to exclude VTE.
whyUse: Age × 10 µg/L FEU (age × 0.01 mg/L) after age 50 improves specificity without major sensitivity loss (ADJUST-PE).

name: Primary Care Rule for DVT (Oudega)
whenToUse: Primary care / outpatient suspected lower-extremity DVT when ultrasound access is gated by risk.
whyUse: Score ≤3 safely withholds ultrasound in validation studies; integrates D-dimer into the rule.

name: Ottawa SAH Rule
whenToUse: Alert patients ≥15 years with new severe nontraumatic headache peaking within 1 hour — SAH not already confirmed.
whyUse: High sensitivity rule: any criterion positive → investigate; all negative → SAH extremely unlikely.

actions: No SAH workup if eligibility met

name: EGSYS Syncope Score
whenToUse: Adults with syncope when estimating likelihood of cardiac etiology.
whyUse: Point score from history distinguishing cardiac vs non-cardiac syncope (EGSYS).

name: OESIL Syncope Risk Score
whenToUse: Adult ED syncope patients for simple mortality risk banding.
whyUse: Four binary items; scores ≥2 associate with higher 12-month mortality in derivation.

name: ROSE Rule (Syncope)
whenToUse: Adult ED patients with syncope for short-term serious outcome risk (BRACES mnemonic).
whyUse: Any positive ROSE criterion classifies higher risk; includes BNP which other rules omit.

name: Boston Syncope Rule (Simplified)
whenToUse: ED syncope disposition when applying Boston rule risk categories.
whyUse: High-sensitivity admission rule based on signs of cardiac/ischemic/conduction/volume/family risk.

name: Delta Troponin Interpreter (Educational)
whenToUse: Chest pain pathways with serial troponins when assessing rise/fall consistent with acute myocardial injury.
whyUse: Absolute deltas matter more than relative % at low hs-Tn levels; thresholds are assay-specific — this tool teaches the concepts.

name: de Winter T-Wave Pattern Helper
whenToUse: Anterior ischemic symptoms with upsloping ST depression and tall peaked precordial T waves.
whyUse: de Winter pattern is an occlusion MI equivalent — activate reperfusion without waiting for classic STEMI.

name: STEMI Equivalent Patterns Checklist
whenToUse: Suspected acute coronary occlusion when classic STEMI mm criteria are absent or subtle.
whyUse: Bundles high-yield OMI patterns so none are missed while waiting for biomarker evolution.

name: Harris–Benedict BMR (Revised)
whenToUse: Estimate resting energy needs for nutrition planning when a predictive equation is appropriate.
whyUse: Classic BMR equations; still used educationally (Mifflin–St Jeor often preferred in modern practice).

actions: Consider Mifflin–St Jeor or measured REE
Reassess with weight trend and intake

name: Mifflin–St Jeor REE/BMR
whenToUse: Preferred common predictive equation for resting energy needs in many ambulatory adults.
whyUse: Generally more accurate than Harris–Benedict for contemporary populations.

actions: Combine with protein targets and resistance training counseling

name: Daily Protein Needs
whenToUse: Setting protein goals for healthy adults, illness, or recovery when weight-based targets apply.
whyUse: Quick g/day from common g/kg ranges used in nutrition support.

actions: Consider nitrogen balance or urea kinetics

name: Nitrogen Balance
whenToUse: Assessing catabolic state / adequacy of protein delivery with 24-h UUN collection.
whyUse: Simple bedside estimate of anabolic vs catabolic nitrogen status.

name: Urea Reduction Ratio (URR)
whenToUse: Session adequacy estimate from pre- and post-dialysis BUN.
whyUse: Simple adequacy metric; target often URR ≥65% for thrice-weekly HD (with caveats).

name: spKt/V (Daugirdas Second Generation)
whenToUse: Estimating single-pool dialysis dose from pre/post BUN, session length, UF, and post weight.
whyUse: Standard clinical approximation of urea kinetic dose for thrice-weekly HD.

name: 4-2-1 Hourly Maintenance Fluids
whenToUse: Quick hourly maintenance rate from weight when daily 100/50/20 math is not needed.
whyUse: Bedside mnemonic identical in intent to Holliday–Segar hourly delivery.

actions: Choose isotonic fluid per local/AAP guidance

name: Brooke Burn Fluid Formula (Modified)
whenToUse: Alternative to Parkland for burn shock resuscitation planning (still titrate to endpoints).
whyUse: Lower starting crystalloid estimate (2 mL/kg/%TBSA) than classic Parkland 4 mL; used in some burn protocols.

name: Lund–Browder TBSA (Simplified)
whenToUse: Pediatric or age-sensitive TBSA estimates when rule-of-nines is too crude.
whyUse: Head and leg proportions change with age; Lund–Browder is the preferred chart method.

actions: Palm method (~1% patient palm) for patchy burns

name: Temperature °C ↔ °F
whenToUse: Unit conversion for vital signs and labs reported in different systems.
whyUse: Avoids mis-triage from °C/°F confusion.

name: Weight lb ↔ kg
whenToUse: Drug dosing and charting when weight units differ.

actions: Confirm scale unit before mg/kg calculations

name: Length in ↔ cm
whenToUse: Height entry for IBW/BMI and pediatric length conversions.
whyUse: Exact factor 1 in = 2.54 cm.

name: Pressure mmHg ↔ kPa
whenToUse: ABG or BP values reported in kPa vs mmHg.
whyUse: 1 mmHg ≈ 0.133322 kPa; 1 kPa ≈ 7.50062 mmHg.

actions: Keep PaO₂/PaCO₂ unit-consistent with local normals

name: Energy kcal ↔ kJ
whenToUse: Food labels and nutrition prescriptions across unit systems.
whyUse: 1 kcal (thermochemical) = 4.184 kJ.

actions: Pair energy targets with protein and micronutrient goals

name: Number Needed to Treat (NNT)
whenToUse: Translating trial event rates into a bedside benefit metric.
whyUse: Communicates how many patients need treatment to prevent one additional event.

actions: Compare to NNH for net benefit

name: Number Needed to Harm (NNH)
whenToUse: Quantifying how many patients are treated for one additional adverse event.
whyUse: Balances NNT discussions with harm metrics.

actions: Discuss severity of prevented vs caused events

name: ARR and RRR
whenToUse: Interpreting binary trial outcomes (benefit direction).
whyUse: ARR drives NNT; RRR can look large when baseline risk is small.

actions: Emphasize absolute benefit for shared decisions

actions: Combine with LR via Fagan pathway

name: PPV / NPV from Sens, Spec, Prevalence
whenToUse: When sens/spec are known and you need predictive values at a given prevalence.
whyUse: PPV/NPV depend strongly on prevalence; sens/spec alone mislead.

name: Diagnostic Odds Ratio (DOR)
whenToUse: Single-number summary of diagnostic test discrimination (meta-analysis / education).
whyUse: DOR = (TP/FN)/(FP/TN) = LR+/LR−; higher favors better overall discrimination.

actions: Report sens/spec and LRs alongside DOR
Avoid ranking tests by DOR alone

name: 95% CI for a Proportion (Wilson)
whenToUse: Quick CI around a success proportion (e.g., response rate x/n).
whyUse: Wilson interval behaves better than simple Wald p±1.96√(p(1-p)/n) near 0 or 1.

actions: Consider exact binomial CI for small samples

name: Sample Size for a Proportion (Rough)
whenToUse: Quick planning estimate for a descriptive proportion study.
whyUse: n ≈ Z²p(1−p)/E² before software simulation / exact methods.

actions: Specify primary endpoint and analysis clearly

name: Anemia MCV Classification
whenToUse: First branch point after finding low hemoglobin/hematocrit.
whyUse: MCV directs differential (iron/thalassemia vs bleed/hemolysis/CKD vs B12/folate/etc.).

actions: Consider Hb electrophoresis if thalassemia suspected

name: RDW + MCV Anemia Pattern
whenToUse: CBC differential hints when both MCV and RDW are available.
whyUse: Classic teaching tables pair high/normal RDW with micro/normo/macro MCV.

name: Revised IPI (R-IPI, DLBCL)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed DLBCL / aggressive B-NHL treated in the rituximab era for OS risk groups.
whyUse: Reclassifies classic IPI into three clinically useful strata (very good / good / poor) better aligned with R-CHOP outcomes.

name: CNS-IPI (DLBCL CNS Relapse Risk)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed DLBCL when deciding CNS staging intensity and prophylaxis strategies.
whyUse: Stratifies 2-year CNS relapse risk into low / intermediate / high groups to support prophylaxis discussions.

actions: Review additional high-risk sites (testis, breast, epidural)
Consider LP / MRI if neurologic symptoms

name: DIPSS (Primary Myelofibrosis)
whenToUse: Primary myelofibrosis for risk stratification at diagnosis or later (dynamic).
whyUse: Hb-weighted model predicts survival and frames transplant / JAK inhibitor discussions.

name: DIPSS-plus (Myelofibrosis)
whenToUse: Primary myelofibrosis when karyotype, platelet count, and transfusion status are known.
whyUse: Improves discrimination over DIPSS alone and better identifies highest-risk patients.

name: Sokal Score (CML)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed chronic-phase CML before or at TKI start (historical risk grouping).
whyUse: Still reported in trials and labels; frames baseline risk though ELTS is preferred for TKI-era long-term survival.

name: Hasford Score (Euro / CML)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed chronic-phase CML risk stratification (historical Euro score).
whyUse: Complementary to Sokal; developed in interferon era and still cited alongside Sokal/EUTOS/ELTS.

name: EUTOS Score (CML)
whenToUse: Chronic-phase CML at diagnosis when a simple spleen + basophil score is desired.
whyUse: Minimal inputs; originally validated for CCyR probability on imatinib (not identical to ELTS long-term survival model).

actions: Ensure adherence and drug interactions review
Also compute ELTS if long-term OS risk needed

name: ISS (Multiple Myeloma)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma staging (pair with R-ISS when cytogenetics/LDH available).
whyUse: Simple, widely validated three-stage system that correlates with overall survival.

name: R-ISS (Revised Myeloma Staging)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma when ISS stage, LDH, and FISH results are available.
whyUse: Improves prognostic separation versus ISS alone in the novel-agent era.

actions: Confirm CA by iFISH on plasma cells

name: Durie-Salmon Stage (Simplified)
whenToUse: Historical staging context or when comparing older literature; ISS/R-ISS preferred for modern prognosis.
whyUse: Captures tumor burden concept (anemia, calcium, bone disease, M-protein) plus creatinine substage A/B.

name: Rai Staging (CLL)
whenToUse: Staging newly diagnosed or progressing CLL in systems that use Rai (common in North America).
whyUse: Simple exam/lab stages correlate with survival and are used with CLL-IPI for treatment timing discussions.

name: Binet Staging (CLL)
whenToUse: CLL staging using lymphoid area count and hemoglobin/platelet thresholds (common in Europe).
whyUse: Three-group system that is quick at the bedside and used in CLL-IPI stage component definitions.

name: CLL-IPI
whenToUse: CLL prognostic counseling when molecular/FISH and β2-microglobulin results are available.
whyUse: Integrates genetics with clinical factors for four OS risk groups in the chemoimmunotherapy era (still used with BTKi/BCL2 contexts).

actions: BTK or BCL2-based therapy preferred over CIT
Confirm IWCLL treatment indication before starting therapy

name: PIT (Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed PTCL (especially PTCL-NOS) risk stratification.
whyUse: Four-factor model tailored to PTCL; simpler alternative to IPI in T-cell lymphoma literature.

actions: Confirm subtype (PTCL-NOS vs AITL vs ALCL, etc.)
CD30, ALK, TFH markers as relevant

name: Age-Adjusted IPI (aaIPI)
whenToUse: Aggressive NHL / DLBCL in patients age ≤60 for risk grouping without the age factor.
whyUse: Focuses on LDH, performance status, and stage — the dominant factors in younger adults.

name: MIPI (Mantle Cell Lymphoma)
whenToUse: Newly diagnosed mantle cell lymphoma risk stratification.
whyUse: MCL-specific index superior to IPI for this disease; guides intensity discussions with MIPI-c (Ki-67) when available.

actions: Discuss BTKi-based vs chemoimmunotherapy era options

name: BSA (Mosteller Formula)
whenToUse: When BSA is needed for mg/m² dosing, cardiac index, or other indexed parameters.
whyUse: Simple square-root formula widely accepted and easy to verify at the bedside.

name: CISNE (Febrile Neutropenia)
whenToUse: Adult solid-tumor (and selected) patients with febrile neutropenia who appear clinically stable at presentation.
whyUse: Helps identify who remains high-risk for complications despite apparent stability; complements MASCC.

actions: Consider oral outpatient pathway if protocol allows
IV antipseudomonal coverage until stability clear

name: DAS28 (RA Disease Activity)
whenToUse: Rheumatoid arthritis treat-to-target monitoring with tender/swollen joint counts and acute-phase reactant.
whyUse: Standard composite endpoint for remission/LDA/MDA/HDA classification in RA trials and clinics.

name: CDAI (RA)
whenToUse: RA disease activity assessment when labs are unavailable or a purely clinical composite is preferred.
whyUse: Simple sum of joint counts and global assessments; same-day scoring without ESR/CRP.

name: SDAI (RA)
whenToUse: RA monitoring when tender/swollen counts, dual globals, and CRP are available.
whyUse: ACR/EULAR-endorsed composite; remission cutoff commonly used in trials and practice.

name: BASDAI (Ankylosing Spondylitis)
whenToUse: Axial spondyloarthritis / AS disease activity monitoring and biologic eligibility discussions.
whyUse: Standard PRO composite; BASDAI ≥4 often denotes active disease in pathways and trials.

name: SLEDAI-2K (Total Interpretation)
whenToUse: When SLEDAI-2K has been scored from the 24 descriptors and a total needs band interpretation.
whyUse: Standard lupus activity index used in trials and clinics; this helper maps totals to severity strata.

name: PASI (Total Interpretation)
whenToUse: When PASI has been calculated from region scores and a severity band is needed for documentation or systemic therapy discussions.
whyUse: PASI is the standard psoriasis severity composite in trials (PASI-75/90 responses).

name: Arterial Oxygen Content (CaO₂)
whenToUse: Shock, anemia, hypoxemia workups when quantifying blood O₂ carrying capacity.
whyUse: CaO₂ is the content term in DO₂ and O₂ extraction calculations.

actions: Treat anemia only per restrictive transfusion thresholds unless active ischemia/bleeding
Combine with CO for DO₂ and with CvO₂ for extraction ratio

name: Mixed Venous Oxygen Content (CvO₂)
whenToUse: When mixed venous (or sometimes central venous as surrogate) gases available for O₂ balance.
whyUse: Needed for AV O₂ difference, O₂ER, and Fick-based calculations.

actions: Assess shock type and cardiac output
Optimize DO₂ (preload, inotropes, oxygenation, Hb per thresholds)
Reduce VO₂ when appropriate (fever, work of breathing, agitation)

name: Oxygen Extraction Ratio (O₂ER)
whenToUse: Shock / high-risk ICU when arterial and mixed venous contents (or saturations with shared Hb) are known.
whyUse: Summarizes balance between O₂ delivery and consumption; rises when delivery falls or demand rises.

nextSteps.condition: O₂ER low / SvO₂ high in shock
actions: Consider distributive shock or impaired utilization
Source control and sepsis care if infection

name: Ventilation Index (VI)
whenToUse: Ventilated patients (classically pediatric) when grading ventilatory support intensity.
whyUse: Integrates rate, driving pressure component (PIP−PEEP), and CO₂; higher VI = more intense support.

actions: Consider advanced therapies per local criteria if refractory

name: Rapid Shallow Breathing Index (RSBI)
whenToUse: Spontaneous breathing trial assessment for readiness to wean/extubate.
whyUse: Simple bedside predictor; RSBI <105 breaths/min/L associated with weaning success in classic studies.

actions: Assess cuff leak/airway protection as indicated
Plan extubation with post-extubation support strategy
Address volume overload, weakness, secretions, acidosis

name: Predicted Body Weight (ARDSNet PBW)
whenToUse: Any adult on invasive ventilation when setting mL/kg tidal volume (especially ARDS).
whyUse: Vt is dosed by PBW, not actual weight, to avoid overdistension in obesity.

name: ARDS Tidal Volume Target (6 mL/kg PBW)
whenToUse: Setting or checking Vt on invasive ventilation for ARDS or prevention of VILI.
whyUse: Low tidal volume (~6 mL/kg PBW) reduces mortality in ARDS versus traditional 12 mL/kg.

name: Driving Pressure (ΔP)
whenToUse: Volume- or pressure-controlled ventilation with measurable end-inspiratory plateau.
whyUse: ΔP is strongly associated with ARDS mortality; aim often ≤15 cm H₂O when feasible.

actions: Lower Vt if Pplat allows room on gas exchange

name: Static Respiratory Compliance (Cstat)
whenToUse: Passive ventilated patients with reliable plateau pressure.
whyUse: Tracks stiffness of lung/chest wall; falling Cstat suggests edema, fibrosis, abdominal hypertension, mainstem intubation.

actions: CXR / ultrasound for edema, pneumothorax, mainstem tube
Reassess fluid balance and ARDS therapies

name: Airway Resistance (Raw)
whenToUse: Passive volume-cycled breath with constant flow and plateau hold.
whyUse: Separates resistive load (ETT, bronchospasm, secretions) from elastic load (Pplat).

actions: Suction / check ETT position and biting
Consider larger ETT only if indicated; avoid auto-PEEP with adequate expiratory time

name: Respiratory Time Constant (τ)
whenToUse: When Raw and compliance are known or measured; planning expiratory time in obstruction.
whyUse: ~3 time constants empty ~95% of tidal volume; guides risk of air trapping.

actions: Reduce respiratory rate / I:E toward longer expiration
Permissive hypercapnia if needed for safety

name: NEWS (Original National Early Warning Score)
whenToUse: Adult ward monitoring where original NEWS (not NEWS2) is the local standard.
whyUse: Standardized aggregate score for acute illness severity and escalation.

actions: Hourly observations minimum per local policy

name: Vasoactive-Inotropic Score (VIS)
whenToUse: Quantifying pharmacologic cardiovascular support (pediatric cardiac ICU classic; also adult research).
whyUse: Single number comparing support intensity across dopamine, epi, norepi, milrinone, vasopressin, etc.

actions: Reassess volume status and cardiac function
Escalate monitoring / mechanical support pathways as indicated

name: Lactate Clearance (%)
whenToUse: Serial lactate monitoring during sepsis or shock resuscitation.
whyUse: Improving lactate is associated with better outcomes; used as a resuscitation trend marker.

actions: Reassess volume, cardiac output, source control
Consider occult hypoperfusion or liver failure limiting clearance

name: Base Deficit Severity Class
whenToUse: Trauma, hemorrhage, or shock when ABG/VBG base excess is available.
whyUse: Base deficit correlates with oxygen debt, transfusion need, and mortality in trauma cohorts.

actions: Avoid over-focusing on buffer therapy alone without perfusion restoration

name: SALT Mass Casualty Triage
whenToUse: Mass casualty incidents using SALT framework (US NHTSA/CDC-endorsed model).
whyUse: Provides common language: Immediate, Delayed, Minimal, Expectant, Dead.

name: JumpSTART Pediatric MCI Triage
whenToUse: Pediatric casualties in MCI when JumpSTART is the operational system.
whyUse: Modifies START for pediatric respiratory physiology (RR limits, airway + ventilation step).

name: Nursing Delirium Screening Scale (Nu-DESC)
whenToUse: Ward or ICU nursing screening for delirium each shift.
whyUse: Brief observational tool; score ≥2 suggests possible delirium needing further assessment.

name: Riker Sedation-Agitation Scale (SAS)
whenToUse: ICU sedation/agitation charting when SAS is the unit standard (alternative to RASS).
whyUse: Simple ordinal scale to titrate sedatives toward calm, arousable targets (often SAS 3–4).

actions: Rule out pain, hypoxia, full bladder, delirium

name: Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (ICDSC)
whenToUse: ICU patients when ICDSC is the preferred delirium tool (alternative to CAM-ICU).
whyUse: Captures fluctuating symptoms over the nursing shift; continuous score allows trend tracking.

actions: Identify reversible causes (infection, hypoxia, metabolic, drugs, withdrawal)

name: Braden Scale for Predicting Pressure Sore Risk
whenToUse: Hospitalized adults for pressure injury risk stratification and care planning.
whyUse: Most widely used validated pressure ulcer risk tool in North America.

actions: Offload heels; inspect skin each shift

name: Waterlow Pressure Ulcer Risk Score
whenToUse: Adults when Waterlow is the institutional pressure injury risk tool.
whyUse: Includes build, skin type, sex/age, continence, mobility, nutrition, and special risk factors.

name: Norton Pressure Sore Risk Scale
whenToUse: Adults when Norton is used for pressure injury risk (historical and some current settings).
whyUse: Simple 5-item scale; ≤14 commonly indicates increased risk.

name: MUST Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool
whenToUse: Adults in hospital or community for malnutrition risk screening.
whyUse: Rapid validated screen that triggers care pathways (food-first, dietitian, monitoring).

name: RACE Scale (Prehospital LVO)
whenToUse: Suspected acute ischemic stroke in the field or ED triage when routing to endovascular-capable centers is considered.
whyUse: Simple cortical + motor scale; RACE ≥5 suggests high likelihood of LVO and may support direct transport to thrombectomy centers.

actions: Preferential routing to EVT-capable center if protocol allows

name: LAMS (Los Angeles Motor Scale)
whenToUse: Rapid field or triage motor assessment when large-vessel occlusion is a concern.
whyUse: Very brief motor-only LVO screen; LAMS ≥4 commonly associated with higher LVO probability.

actions: Do not delay thrombolysis pathway if eligible

name: C-STAT (Cincinnati Stroke Triage Assessment Tool)
whenToUse: Prehospital or triage LVO screening with minimal items.
whyUse: Quick weighted scale; C-STAT ≥2 commonly used as LVO-positive screen.

name: FAST-ED Scale
whenToUse: Prehospital triage when deciding transport destination for suspected large-vessel occlusion.
whyUse: Balances facial, arm, speech, eye deviation, and denial/neglect items linked to cortical LVO.

actions: Route to comprehensive stroke / EVT center per protocol

name: FUNC Score (ICH Functional Outcome)
whenToUse: Spontaneous ICH when discussing 90-day functional independence probability (not mortality alone).
whyUse: Complements ICH Score (mortality) with functional outcome estimates based on age, GCS, volume, location, and cognition.

actions: Discuss prognosis with ranges, not certainties

name: CTA Spot Sign Helper (ICH Expansion)
whenToUse: Spontaneous ICH with CTA performed or planned when assessing risk of hematoma expansion.
whyUse: Structures recognition of spot sign and companion clinical risk factors linked to growth and poor outcome.

nextSteps.condition: Spot sign positive or high risk

name: WFNS SAH Grade
whenToUse: Confirmed or highly suspected aneurysmal SAH for standardized clinical severity grading.
whyUse: Widely used international grade linking GCS and focal motor deficit to outcome; complements Hunt-Hess and Fisher grades.

name: SAH Vasospasm / DCI Risk Window
whenToUse: Aneurysmal SAH care planning for monitoring intensity during the DCI-risk period.
whyUse: DCI risk is time-dependent (peaks ~days 7–10, window ~3–14) and higher with thick blood / high modified Fisher grades.

actions: Low threshold for imaging on change

name: TBI Severity by GCS
whenToUse: Initial TBI severity stratification after primary survey and GCS assessment.
whyUse: Universal mild (13–15) / moderate (9–12) / severe (≤8) bands drive imaging, airway, and disposition pathways.

name: SCAT Symptom Severity Score
whenToUse: Sideline or clinic concussion assessment after administering the SCAT symptom checklist.
whyUse: Quantifies symptom burden for baseline comparison, recovery tracking, and return-to-play decisions.

actions: Remove from play same day if concussion suspected

name: Graduated Return-to-Play (Concussion)
whenToUse: Planning and documenting stepwise return to sport after concussion once return-to-learn is underway/stable.
whyUse: Standard consensus stages reduce premature full-contact return and symptom exacerbation.

name: 4AT Delirium Screen
whenToUse: Bedside screening for delirium in ED, wards, or older adults with acute illness.
whyUse: Brief, no special training beyond the tool; ≥4 suggests possible delirium requiring full assessment.

actions: Workup: infection, metabolic, hypoxia, urinary retention, meds
Non-pharm delirium care; avoid benzos unless alcohol/benzo withdrawal

name: bCAM Simplified (Brief Confusion Assessment)
whenToUse: ED or ward delirium assessment using bCAM/CAM feature logic after attention testing.
whyUse: Structured binary algorithm aligned with CAM: inattention + acute change plus either altered LOC or disorganized thinking.

name: ACE-III Total Score Interpreter
whenToUse: When ACE-III has been administered and domain/total scores are available for interpretation.
whyUse: Broader than MMSE/MoCA alone; total cutoffs aid dementia vs MCI triage (education-dependent).

name: IQCODE (Informant Cognitive Decline)
whenToUse: When an informant rates change in cognition over ~10 years and average IQCODE is available.
whyUse: Useful when patient testing is limited; captures longitudinal decline better than a single cross-sectional screen.

name: AD8 Dementia Screening Interview
whenToUse: Brief dementia screen in primary care, neurology, or geriatrics using informant-preferred AD8.
whyUse: Two or more “yes” responses suggest cognitive impairment warranting further evaluation.

name: Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15)
whenToUse: Depression screening in older adults when GDS-15 total is available.
whyUse: Yes/no format well tolerated in elderly; validated cutoffs for mild to severe depression ranges.

name: Cornell Scale for Depression in Dementia
whenToUse: When depression is suspected in someone with cognitive impairment and CSDD has been rated.
whyUse: Uses caregiver + clinician observations; better suited than self-report PHQ when insight/memory is limited.

actions: Rule out delirium, pain, constipation, meds

name: Zarit Caregiver Burden (Short Total)
whenToUse: Assessing caregiver strain in dementia or chronic neurologic illness after administering a Zarit form.
whyUse: Quantifies burden to trigger support services, respite, and depression screening of caregivers.

name: PSQI Global Score (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality)
whenToUse: When PSQI has been scored and global sleep quality needs interpretation.
whyUse: Standard research/clinical metric of past-month sleep quality; global >5 indicates poor sleep.

name: IRLS (Restless Legs Severity)
whenToUse: Quantify RLS symptom severity after clinical diagnosis of restless legs syndrome.
whyUse: Standard 10-item severity scale for baseline and treatment response.

actions: Serum ferritin (often treat if <50–75 µg/L per guidelines/context)
Alpha-2-delta ligands or other agents per severity and comorbidities

name: PC-PTSD-5 Screen
whenToUse: Primary care or general medical screening when lifetime traumatic event exposure is endorsed.
whyUse: Ultra-brief DSM-5 PTSD screen; ≥3 positive items suggests further PTSD assessment.

name: CIWA-B (Benzodiazepine Withdrawal) Simplified
whenToUse: Monitoring benzodiazepine withdrawal severity when a CIWA-B (or local benzo-withdrawal) total is charted.
whyUse: Provides structured severity bands analogous to alcohol CIWA for taper/monitoring decisions — not a substitute for the full instrument item list.

name: Opioid Risk Tool (ORT)
whenToUse: Before initiating chronic opioid therapy for non-cancer pain to stratify misuse risk.
whyUse: Brief weighted checklist; low / moderate / high risk bands guide monitoring intensity (not a ban on treatment).

actions: If prescribing: small quantities, frequent visits, UDS
Addiction medicine / pain specialist referral as needed

name: ADA Type 2 Diabetes Risk Test
whenToUse: Adults in primary care or community settings to identify who may need glucose testing.
whyUse: Simple validated point score; higher scores warrant diagnostic testing (A1c, FPG, or OGTT).

name: FINDRISC Diabetes Risk Score
whenToUse: Adults for opportunistic type 2 diabetes risk stratification and prevention counseling.
whyUse: Widely validated non-invasive score; high scores prompt OGTT/A1c and lifestyle programs.

name: Diabetes Diagnostic Category (A1c/FPG/OGTT)
whenToUse: When classifying glycemic status from one or more diagnostic tests.
whyUse: Aligns results with ADA diagnostic cutoffs; flags discordant tests needing confirmation.

name: ADA Hypoglycemia Level
whenToUse: Documenting or triaging hypoglycemic events in people with diabetes.
whyUse: Standardized levels guide treatment intensity, education, and regimen review.

name: Insulin Sensitivity Factor (Rule of 1800/1500)
whenToUse: Initial estimate of correction factor when designing or revising a basal–bolus plan.
whyUse: Rule-of-thumb from total daily dose; must be individualized with SMBG/CGM.

name: Insulin-to-Carb Ratio (Rule of 500)
whenToUse: Estimating grams of carbohydrate covered by 1 unit of mealtime insulin.
whyUse: Starting point for carbohydrate counting regimens; refine with postprandial data.

name: Insulin Correction Dose
whenToUse: Estimating units of rapid-acting insulin to correct hyperglycemia above target.
whyUse: Standard formula for correction boluses; combine carefully with meal bolus and IOB.

actions: Check for illness, steroids, pump failure

name: Weight-Based Total Daily Insulin Estimate
whenToUse: Rough starting TDD estimate for insulin-naive or regimen redesign (supervised).
whyUse: Weight-based ranges provide a safe starting framework before titration.

name: Basal–Bolus Split from TDD
whenToUse: Designing MDI or reviewing pump basal total from known TDD.
whyUse: Classic 50/50 starting split; adjustable for dawn phenomenon or high carb intake.

actions: Increase prandial share or strengthen ICR

name: Steroid Hyperglycemia Risk / Expected Rise Helper
whenToUse: Patients starting or escalating systemic glucocorticoids, with or without known diabetes.
whyUse: Steroids raise postprandial glucose disproportionately; anticipatory monitoring and treatment planning reduce complications.

name: Thyroid Function Pattern Interpreter
whenToUse: When TSH and free T4 are available and a pattern-based differential is needed.
whyUse: Rapid pattern recognition guides next labs (T3, antibodies, imaging, pituitary workup).

name: Levothyroxine Dose Estimate (Adult)
whenToUse: Estimating full replacement dose in adults; use lower starts in elderly or cardiac disease.
whyUse: ≈1.6 µg/kg ideal/actual weight is a common full-replacement starting estimate in healthy adults.

name: PTH with Calcium Pattern Interpreter
whenToUse: Abnormal calcium evaluation when PTH is available.
whyUse: PTH–calcium pairing is the core branch point for parathyroid vs non-parathyroid disorders.

name: Vitamin D Status (25-OH D)
whenToUse: Interpreting serum 25-OH vitamin D results.
whyUse: Common cutoffs guide repletion vs maintenance; lab units and targets vary slightly by society.

actions: Repletion (e.g., weekly high-dose then daily maintenance)

name: FRAX-Style Major Risk Factor Checklist (Educational)
whenToUse: Quick bedside tally of clinical risk factors before formal FRAX or densitometry decisions.
whyUse: Highlights who needs DXA, fall prevention, and treatment discussion. Does not replace official FRAX tool.

name: DXA T-Score Interpretation (WHO)
whenToUse: Interpreting central DXA T-scores in postmenopausal women and men ≥50 years.
whyUse: WHO categories drive labeling; treatment also considers fracture history and FRAX.

actions: Dental/GI clearance if needed for agents

name: WHO BMI Classification
whenToUse: When BMI is already calculated and category labeling is needed.
whyUse: Standard adult WHO cutoffs for underweight through class III obesity.

name: Pediatric BMI Percentile Interpretation
whenToUse: When BMI percentile from growth charts/EMR is available for ages 2–19.
whyUse: Pediatric weight status uses percentiles, not adult BMI cutoffs.

actions: Screen BP, lipids, glucose as indicated

name: Fatty Liver Index (FLI)
whenToUse: Noninvasive estimate of fatty liver probability in adults when imaging not yet done.
whyUse: FLI <30 rules out and ≥60 rules in steatosis with reasonable accuracy in validation cohorts.

name: Hepatic Steatosis Index (HSI)
whenToUse: Simple lab-based screen for NAFLD/MASLD steatosis risk.
whyUse: HSI <30 rules out and >36 rules in steatosis in original Korean derivation.

name: NIDA Quick Screen
whenToUse: Primary care or general medical visits for brief substance use screening.
whyUse: Positive screen prompts full NIDA-Modified ASSIST and brief intervention.

name: Tobacco Quit Readiness (Stages of Change)
whenToUse: When counseling patients who use tobacco to match intervention to readiness.
whyUse: Tailors 5A/5R messages; avoids one-size-fit-all advice.

name: ACC/AHA Blood Pressure Classification
whenToUse: Adults with standardized BP readings for category labeling (not a diagnosis alone).
whyUse: 2017 ACC/AHA thresholds guide lifestyle intensity and treatment discussions.

name: Pulse Pressure
whenToUse: From paired systolic and diastolic BP when assessing pulse pressure width.
whyUse: Wide PP associated with arterial stiffness and CV risk; narrow PP may reflect low stroke volume.

actions: Treat isolated systolic HTN per guidelines

name: EHRA AF Symptom Score
whenToUse: Patients with AF to grade symptom burden and guide rhythm-control discussions.
whyUse: Standardized language for AF symptom severity used in ESC AF guidelines and trials.

name: CCS Angina Classification
whenToUse: Patients with stable ischemic heart disease / angina to document functional limitation.
whyUse: Universal language for angina severity used in trials, guidelines, and revascularization discussions.

actions: Risk stratify with noninvasive testing as appropriate

name: ACC/AHA Heart Failure Stages
whenToUse: Adults at risk for or with structural heart disease / clinical HF to stage disease continuum.
whyUse: Stages drive prevention and therapy intensity; distinct from NYHA functional class.

actions: Screen for structural disease when indicated

name: HFrEF GDMT Optimization Checklist
whenToUse: Patients with HFrEF (typically LVEF ≤40%) to audit GDMT completeness.
whyUse: Four-pillar therapy reduces mortality; checklist highlights gaps for titration visits.

actions: Use low-dose multi-drug start when appropriate

name: Sokolow–Lyon LVH Voltage
whenToUse: ECG interpretation when LVH is suspected (hypertension, aortic stenosis, cardiomyopathy screening).
whyUse: Classic, simple voltage criterion; limited sensitivity but good specificity when met.

name: Cornell Voltage LVH Criteria
whenToUse: ECG LVH assessment using Cornell voltage (often more sensitive than Sokolow–Lyon alone).
whyUse: Sex-specific thresholds improve performance; Cornell product adds QRS duration.

name: Corrected QT (Rautaharju)
whenToUse: QT correction when an alternative linear/rate formula to Bazett is desired.
whyUse: Rautaharju correction is less biased than Bazett at higher heart rates in many comparisons.

name: JT / JTc Interval
whenToUse: Wide QRS (bundle branch block, pacing, ventricular conduction delay) when assessing repolarization.
whyUse: QTc includes QRS duration; JT/JTc isolates repolarization and may better reflect TdP risk with wide QRS.

actions: Telemetry if very prolonged or symptomatic

name: Warfarin INR Goal by Indication
whenToUse: Selecting or verifying target INR for warfarin therapy.
whyUse: INR targets differ for mechanical valves vs AF/VTE; mistakes cause thrombosis or bleeding.

actions: Bridge per bleeding/thrombosis risk when interrupting

name: DOAC Renal Dose Helper
whenToUse: Adults starting or reviewing DOAC dose for AF or VTE when kidney function is known.
whyUse: Renal dosing errors are a leading cause of DOAC under/overdose.

name: Enoxaparin Dosing Helper
whenToUse: Adults needing LMWH prophylaxis or treatment dose planning (verify indication-specific protocols).
whyUse: Weight- and renal-adjusted dosing reduces under/over-anticoagulation.

actions: Consider UFH infusion if rapidly reversible agent preferred
Prefer actual body weight for treatment

name: ACS Unfractionated Heparin Bolus/Infusion
whenToUse: Adults with ACS when initiating unfractionated heparin per weight-based protocol.
whyUse: Weight-based dosing with caps is standard; errors in bolus/infusion are common.

name: Lipoprotein(a) Risk Bands
whenToUse: When Lp(a) has been measured for primary/secondary prevention risk refinement.
whyUse: Elevated Lp(a) is a causal, genetically determined ASCVD risk enhancer.

actions: Consider lipid specialist if very high or premature ASCVD

name: Apolipoprotein B Risk Bands
whenToUse: When ApoB is available for residual risk assessment or discordance with LDL-C/non-HDL.
whyUse: ApoB counts atherogenic particles and may better reflect risk when discordant with LDL-C.

name: Triglyceride Pancreatitis Risk Bands
whenToUse: Severe hypertriglyceridemia management and patient counseling on pancreatitis risk.
whyUse: Risk rises steeply at very high TG; thresholds guide urgency of therapy.

actions: Insulin/insulin-dextrose or apheresis in selected severe cases per specialist

name: Cardiogenic Shock Clinical Criteria Helper
whenToUse: Suspected cardiogenic shock to structure documentation of hypotension + hypoperfusion ± hemodynamics.
whyUse: Standard criteria improve recognition and shock-team activation language.

name: Hardman Index (Ruptured AAA)
whenToUse: Patients with ruptured AAA being considered for open or endovascular repair risk discussion.
whyUse: Simple bedside score associated with operative mortality; not an absolute futility rule.

name: Glasgow Aneurysm Score
whenToUse: AAA repair risk communication using age and comorbidity points.
whyUse: Simple score correlating with perioperative mortality after aneurysm repair.

name: Duke Activity Status Index (DASI)
whenToUse: Preoperative evaluation or functional capacity estimation when formal exercise testing is unavailable.
whyUse: Validated questionnaire correlating with VO₂ peak; <4 METs flags higher perioperative risk discussions.

actions: Decide on further testing only if it changes management

name: METs Estimate from Activity
whenToUse: Quick bedside estimate of functional capacity from the most vigorous activity the patient can perform.
whyUse: METs frame preoperative and rehab conversations when formal testing is unavailable.

name: Preoperative BNP / NT-proBNP Risk Bands
whenToUse: Elevated risk noncardiac surgery when natriuretic peptides are used for risk stratification.
whyUse: Preop BNP/NT-proBNP independently predict perioperative MI and death.

actions: Consider further cardiac evaluation if it changes plan

name: ARVC Task Force Criteria (Simplified Count)
whenToUse: Structuring suspicion for ARVC/ACM when multiple domain findings exist.
whyUse: Diagnosis requires combining imaging, ECG, arrhythmia, histology, and family history criteria.

actions: Avoid diagnostic over-call from athlete’s heart

name: Schwartz LQTS Diagnostic Score
whenToUse: Suspected congenital LQTS based on ECG, symptoms, and family history.
whyUse: Stratifies low / intermediate / high probability of LQTS before or alongside genetic testing.

name: WPW Accessory Pathway Risk Features
whenToUse: Patients with ventricular preexcitation (WPW pattern) for risk discussion and referral urgency.
whyUse: Certain clinical and electrophysiologic features mark higher risk of rapid conduction and SCD.

actions: Do not give AV nodal blockers in preexcited AF

name: Valvular AF Definition Helper
whenToUse: Choosing anticoagulant class in AF when valve disease is present.
whyUse: DOACs are not appropriate for true valvular AF (moderate–severe MS or mechanical valve); VKA is required.

actions: Set INR goal by valve/MS context

name: Mentzer Index
